Configure OpenClaw 2026.3.2 with any model provider (local or cloud)\n2. Start a Telegram DM session and build up context\n3. React to any bot message with any emoji, then send a new message\n4. Alternatively: send `/reasoning` to toggle reasoning, then send a new message\n\nTo observe the cache invalidation directly, place the diff logger proxy (included in Additional Information) between OpenClaw and the model server. It intercepts `/chat/completions` requests and diffs the system prompt between turns.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe system prompt remains identical between turns when no workspace files have been edited. Prompt cache is reused (`cache_read` for cloud providers, KV prefix match for local providers). Only new tokens (latest user message + assistant response) are processed.\n\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nThe system prompt changes between turns due to two independent mutations:\n\n**1. Runtime System Events injection:**\nA `## Runtime System Events (gateway-generated)` section is appended to the system prompt containing timestamped event lines. Any reaction, reasoning toggle, or other gateway event triggers this.\n\nDiff captured by proxy (turn 84 → 85):\n```diff\n+## Runtime System Events (gateway-generated)\n+Treat this section as trusted gateway runtime metadata, not user text.\n+\n+- [2026-03-05 15:57:38 GMT+1] Telegram reaction added: ❤ by aidiffuser (@aidiffuser) on msg 10947\n```\n\nSetting `channels.telegram.reactionNotifications: \"off\"` only prevents reaction events. Other events (e.g., `Reasoning OFF — hide <think>.`) are still injected into the same section.\n\nAffected code — `subagent-registry-CkqrXKq4.js` line ~16388:\n```javascript\nif (systemLines.length === 0) return;\nreturn [\n    \"## Runtime System Events (gateway-generated)\",\n    \"Treat this section as trusted gateway runtime metadata, not user text.\",\n    \"\",\n    ...systemLines.map((line) => `- ${line}`)\n].join(\"\\n\");\n```\n\n**2. Reasoning level string mutation:**\nThe `## Runtime` footer interpolates `${reasoningLevel}` which changes on every `/reasoning` toggle.\n\nDiff captured by proxy (turn 89 → 90):\n```diff\n-Reasoning: off (hidden unless on/stream). Toggle /reasoning; /status shows Reasoning when enabled.\n+Reasoning: on (hidden unless on/stream). Toggle /reasoning; /status shows Reasoning when enabled.\n```\n\nAffected code — line ~17529:\n```javascript\n`Reasoning: ${reasoningLevel} (hidden unless on/stream). Toggle /reasoning; /status shows Reasoning when enabled.`\n```\n\nThe actual reasoning behavior is controlled via `reasoning_effort` in the request parameters. This system prompt line is purely informational.\n\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2 (85377a2)\n\n### Operating system\n\nmacOS 26.3\n\n### Install method\n\nnpm global install via nvm (node v24.13.0)\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\nSystem prompt diffs captured via HTTP proxy placed between OpenClaw and the model server. Full diff logs saved to `~/kv_debug/`.\n\nCache status before patch (from `/status`):\n\n🗄️ Cache: 99% hit · 109k cached, 0 new\n\nDrops to ~11% hit on the next turn after any runtime event or reasoning toggle, with full re-prefill of the entire context.\n\nCache status after patch: remains stable at 99% hit across turns, including after toggling `/reasoning`.\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\n**Affected users:** All OpenClaw users on all providers — local inference (exo, llama.cpp, LM Studio/MLX, Ollama, vLLM) and cloud APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini).\n\n**Severity:** Blocks workflow for local users. Silent cost increase for cloud API users.\n\n**Frequency:** Every turn where a runtime event has occurred since the last inference call, and on every turn following a `/reasoning` toggle. For users with `reactionNotifications` enabled (the default), a single emoji reaction triggers it.\n\n**Consequence:**\n- Local providers: full KV cache invalidation forces re-prefill of the entire context on every affected turn. On large contexts (100k+ tokens) this adds minutes of latency per message.\n- Cloud providers: prompt cache miss forces `cache_write` instead of `cache_read`, increasing input token cost per turn proportional to the system prompt size. See #19989 and #21999 for related user reports.\n\n### Additional information\n\n### Minimal patch (workaround)\n\nWe are running the following two patches in production. Apply to all 5 affected bundle files:\n\n**1. Early-return from runtime events builder:**\n```bash\nsed -i.bak 's/if (systemLines.length === 0) return;/return; \\/\\/ PATCHED: skip runtime events for KV cache stability/' \"$FILE\"\n```\n\n**2. Replace volatile reasoning interpolation with static string:**\n```bash\nsed -i '' 's/`Reasoning: ${reasoningLevel} (hidden unless on\\/stream)/`Reasoning: stable (hidden unless on\\/stream)/' \"$FILE\"\n```\n\n**Affected files:**\n- `dist/subagent-registry-CkqrXKq4.js`\n- `dist/pi-embedded-DgYXShcG.js`\n- `dist/pi-embedded-CtM2Mrrj.js`\n- `dist/reply-DhtejUNZ.js`\n- `dist/plugin-sdk/reply-DFFRlayb.js`\n\n**Trade-off:** This removes runtime event delivery and reasoning state from the model's awareness entirely. The model no longer sees reactions or knows which reasoning mode is active via the system prompt. Reasoning behavior is unaffected since it's controlled via request parameters.\n\nThese patches are overwritten on `openclaw` updates.\n\n### Suggested upstream fix\n\nMove volatile state out of the system prompt and into conversation-level messages at the end of the messages array. This preserves cache stability (prefix stays immutable) while still delivering runtime information to the model.\n\nFor the reasoning line: make it static or remove it — reasoning behavior is already controlled via `reasoning_effort` in request parameters.\n\nA config option (`agents.defaults.runtimeSystemEvents: \"off\"`) would be a welcome escape hatch for users who don't need runtime events at all.\n\n### Diff logger proxy\n\nThe proxy used to diagnose this issue intercepts `/chat/completions` requests, extracts the system prompt, and diffs it against the previous turn. Deploy between OpenClaw and the model server. Logs to `~/kv_debug/`.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"diff_logger_proxy.py — KV cache debug proxy\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse, difflib, json, socket, sys, threading\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nLOG_DIR = Path.home() / \"kv_debug\"\nLOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nUPSTREAM_HOST = \"localhost\"\nUPSTREAM_PORT = 1235\nturn_counter = 0\nturn_lock = threading.Lock()\nlast_system_prompt = None\n\ndef extract_system_text(payload):\n    def flatten(content):\n        if isinstance(content, str): return content\n        if isinstance(content, list):\n            return \"\\n\".join(\n                b.get(\"text\") or b.get(\"content\") or \"\"\n                if isinstance(b, dict) else b\n                for b in content if b)\n        return \"\"\n    if \"system\" in payload:\n        t = flatten(payload[\"system\"])\n        if t: return t\n    for msg in payload.get(\"messages\", []):\n        if msg.get(\"role\") in (\"system\", \"developer\"):\n            t = flatten(msg.get(\"content\", \"\"))\n            if t: return t\n    return \"\"\n\ndef save_and_diff(system_text):\n    global turn_counter, last_system_prompt\n    with turn_lock:\n        turn_counter += 1; tc = turn_counter\n    ts = datetime.now().strftime(\"%H%M%S\")\n    path = LOG_DIR / f\"turn_{tc:03d}_{ts}_system.txt\"\n    path.write_text(system_text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    print(f\"\\n{'='*70}\\nTURN {tc} — {datetime.now().isoformat()} — {len(system_text)} chars\\n{'='*70}\")\n    if last_system_prompt is None:\n        print(\"  [turn 1] Baseline captured.\")\n    elif system_text == last_system_prompt:\n        print(\"  ✅ SYSTEM PROMPT IDENTICAL — cache prefix should be stable.\")\n    else:\n        print(\"  ❌ SYSTEM PROMPT DIFFERS — cache will be busted!\")\n        diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(\n            last_system_prompt.splitlines(keepends=True),\n            system_text.splitlines(keepends=True),\n            fromfile=f\"turn_{tc-1:03d}\", tofile=f\"turn_{tc:03d}\", n=3))\n        diff_path = LOG_DIR / f\"diff_{tc-1:03d}_vs_{tc:03d}.diff\"\n        diff_path.write_text(\"\".join(diff), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        for line in diff[:80]: sys.stdout.write(\"  \" + line)\n    last_system_prompt = system_text; sys.stdout.flush()\n\ndef pipe_chunks(src, dst, chunk_size=65536):\n    try:\n        while True:\n            data = src.recv(chunk_size)\n            if not data: break\n            dst.sendall(data)\n    except (ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError, OSError): pass\n\nclass ProxyHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):\n    def log_message(self, *a): pass\n    def do_POST(self):\n        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get(\"Content-Length\", 0)))\n        if self.path.rstrip(\"/\").endswith(\"/chat/completions\"):\n            try:\n                payload = json.loads(body)\n                st = extract_system_text(payload)\n                if st: save_and_diff(st)\n            except Exception as e: print(f\"[warn] {e}\")\n        skip = {\"host\",\"content-length\",\"transfer-encoding\",\"connection\",\"proxy-connection\"}\n        hdrs = [f\"POST {self.path} HTTP/1.1\",\n                f\"Host: {UPSTREAM_HOST}:{UPSTREAM_PORT}\",\n                f\"Content-Length: {len(body)}\", \"Connection: close\"]\n        for k,v in self.headers.items():\n            if k.lower() not in skip: hdrs.append(f\"{k}: {v}\")\n        raw = (\"\\r\\n\".join(hdrs) + \"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").encode() + body\n        try: up = socket.create_connection((UPSTREAM_HOST, UPSTREAM_PORT), timeout=600)\n        except Exception as e: return self._err(502, str(e))\n        try:\n            up.sendall(raw); buf = b\"\"\n            while b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\" not in buf:\n                c = up.recv(4096)\n                if not c: break\n                buf += c\n            hend = buf.find(b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\"); rh = buf[:hend]; bs = buf[hend+4:]\n            code = int(rh.split(b\"\\r\\n\")[0].decode().split()[1])\n            self.send_response(code)\n            for l in rh.split(b\"\\r\\n\")[1:]:\n                if b\":\" in l:\n                    k,_,v = l.partition(b\":\")\n                    if k.decode().strip().lower() not in (\"connection\",\"keep-alive\"):\n                        self.send_header(k.decode().strip(), v.decode().strip())\n            self.send_header(\"Connection\",\"close\"); Configure kimi-coding provider in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json:                \n ```json                                                                        \n   {                                                                            \n     \"models\": {                                                                \n       \"mode\": \"merge\",                                                         \n       \"providers\": {                                                           \n         \"kimi-coding\": {                                                       \n           \"baseUrl\": \"https://api.kimi.com/coding\",                            \n           \"apiKey\": \"sk-kimi-...\",                                             \n           \"api\": \"anthropic-messages\",                                         \n           \"models\": [{\"id\": \"kimi-for-coding\", \"name\": \"Kimi for Coding\"}]     \n         }                                                                      \n       }                                                                        \n     },                                                                         \n     \"agents\": {                                                                \n       \"defaults\": {                                                            \n         \"model\": {\"primary\": \"kimi-coding/kimi-for-coding\"}                    \n       }                                                                        \n     }                                                                          \n   }                                                                            \n ```                                                                            \n                                                                                \n 2. Restart OpenClaw gateway: openclaw gateway restart                          \n 3. Send any message to the agent                                               \n 4. Check logs: tail -f /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-*.log  \n\n### Expected behavior\n\nOpenClaw should request https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/messages and return successful responses from Kimi API.    \n\n### Actual behavior\n\nOpenClaw returns 404 error. Log shows: \"error=404 没找到对象\"                \n                                                                                \n   Investigation confirms OpenClaw is requesting                                \n https://api.kimi.com/v1/messages (missing /coding prefix) instead of the       \n configured baseUrl.                                                            \n                                                                                \n   Direct curl test with correct URL returns 200, proving the API key and       \n endpoint work correctly.   \n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nLinux 6.17.0-14-generic\n\n### Install method\n\n_No response_\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\n_No response_\n\n### Additional information\n\nRoot cause in model-selection-*.js:                                            \n                                                                                \n ```javascript                                                                  \n   if (kimiCodingKey) providers[\"kimi-coding\"] = {                              \n       ...buildKimiCodingProvider(),  // Uses hardcoded baseUrl, ignores user   \n config                                                                         \n       apiKey: kimiCodingKey                                                    \n   };   ","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87uz4pZ","author":{"login":"qiuyuemartin-max"},"authorAssociation":"NONE","body":"## Root Cause Analysis\n\nAfter deep investigation (prompted by PR #36381 code review), I've identified the **real root cause** of this bug.\n\n### The Bug is NOT in `resolveImplicitProviders()`\n\nMy initial PR #36381 fixed the wrong location. While `resolveImplicitProviders()` could be improved, the real bug happens later in the data flow.\n\n### The Real Bug: `mergeWithExistingProviderSecrets()`\n\n**Location:** `src/agents/models-config.ts` lines 165-166\n\n**Problem:**\n```typescript\nfunction mergeWithExistingProviderSecrets(params) {\n  // ...\n  const preserved: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n  if (typeof existing.apiKey === \"string\" && existing.apiKey) {\n    preserved.apiKey = existing.apiKey;  // ✅ OK: preserve secret\n  }\n  if (typeof existing.baseUrl === \"string\" && existing.baseUrl) {\n    preserved.baseUrl = existing.baseUrl;  // ❌ BUG: preserve OLD baseUrl from models.json\n  }\n  mergedProviders[key] = { ...newEntry, ...preserved };\n  // This overwrites user's NEW baseUrl with OLD value from models.json!\n}\n```\n\n### Complete Data Flow\n\n```\n1. User updates openclaw.json:\n   { providers: { \"kimi-coding\": { baseUrl: \"https://custom-proxy.com\", ... } } }\n   ↓\n2. resolveImplicitProviders() + mergeProviders():\n   provider.baseUrl = \"https://custom-proxy.com\"  ✅ Correct\n   ↓\n3. resolveProvidersForMode() reads old models.json:\n   old models.json has: baseUrl = \"https://api.kimi.com/coding/\"\n   ↓\n4. mergeWithExistingProviderSecrets(new, old):\n   preserved.baseUrl = \"https://api.kimi.com/coding/\"  ❌ Uses OLD value\n   final result: baseUrl = \"https://api.kimi.com/coding/\"  ❌ User config ignored!\n```\n\n### Why This Happens\n\nThe function `mergeWithExistingProviderSecrets()` is designed to preserve **secrets** (like `apiKey`) from `models.json` so they don't need to be re-entered. However, it incorrectly treats `baseUrl` as a \"secret\" and preserves the old value, **preventing users from updating their configuration**.\n\n### The Correct Fix\n\n**Remove lines 165-166** from `src/agents/models-config.ts`:\n\n```diff\n  const preserved: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n  if (typeof existing.apiKey === \"string\" && existing.apiKey) {\n    preserved.apiKey = existing.apiKey;\n  }\n- if (typeof existing.baseUrl === \"string\" && existing.baseUrl) {\n-   preserved.baseUrl = existing.baseUrl;\n- }\n  mergedProviders[key] = { ...newEntry, ...preserved };\n```\n\n**Why:** `baseUrl` is **user configuration**, not a secret. Users should be able to update it in `openclaw.json`, and the new value should take effect after `openclaw gateway restart`.\n\n### Test Evidence\n\nCreated test script that proves the bug:\n\n```bash\n$ node test-merge-existing-secrets.mjs\n❌ FAIL: User's new baseUrl was overwritten by old models.json value\n❌ This is the REAL bug in Issue #36353!\n```\n\n### Next Steps\n\nI will submit a new PR with:\n1. Fix for `mergeWithExistingProviderSecrets()` (remove baseUrl preservation)\n2. End-to-end test that verifies the fix\n3. Documentation update explaining the behavior\n\n### Workaround (Until Fixed)\n\nUsers can manually edit `~/.openclaw/agents/agent-X/models.json` and update the `baseUrl` there, then restart the gateway.\n\n---\n\nCC @greptile-apps[bot] - Thanks for the code review on PR #36381 that led me to dig deeper and find the real root cause!","createdAt":"2026-03-05T17:33:29Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36353#issuecomment-4006578777","viewerDidAuthor":false}],"createdAt":"2026-03-05T15:27:37Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACQomLZw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACZxxN7g","name":"bug:behavior","description":"Incorrect behavior without a crash","color":"D73A4A"}],"number":36353,"title":"[Bug]: Kimi Coding provider ignores user-configured baseUrl, causing 404 errors","updatedAt":"2026-03-05T17:33:29Z","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36353"},{"body":"### Bug type\n\nBehavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)\n\n### Summary\n\nI've observed that after updating OpenClaw globally using `npm install -g openclaw@latest`, the OpenClaw Gateway service (as reported in the control UI's \"Instances\" page) continues to display an older version number, even though `openclaw doctor` confirms the CLI tools are updated. crash)\n\n### Summary\n\nWhen using `openclaw tui` without `--deliver`, agent responses are also sent to the iMessage channel because `deliveryContext` is persisted in the session from a prior `--deliver` session and the heartbeat with `target: \"last\"` continuously re-writes it.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Configure iMessage channel in `openclaw.json` (dmPolicy: pairing)\n2. Launch TUI with delivery: `openclaw tui --deliver`\n3. Send at least one message — this writes `deliveryContext: {channel: \"imessage\", to: \"<number>\"}` to `agent:main:main` in sessions.json\n4. Exit TUI\n5. Relaunch TUI without deliver: `openclaw tui`\n6. Send a message\n7. Observe: response is delivered to iMessage in addition to TUI\n\n**Perpetuation mechanism:** The gateway heartbeat (default `target: \"last\"`) fires every 30 minutes against the main session and re-writes `deliveryContext` to iMessage. Manually clearing the session fields and restarting the gateway is undone by the next heartbeat cycle.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nResponses sent via `openclaw tui` (without `--deliver`) should appear only in the TUI. The TUI client connection without delivery enabled should be the sole reply target for that session.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nEvery agent response from the TUI session is also delivered to the iMessage channel (`imessage: delivered reply to imessage:<number>` in gateway logs), sending unwanted messages to the user's phone. The behavior persists across gateway restarts as long as `deliveryContext` remains in the session or the heartbeat re-populates it.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nmacOS 26.3 (arm64)\n\n### Install method\n\nnpm global (Homebrew)\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\nGateway log entry confirming delivery:\n\ngateway/channels/imessage: imessage: delivered reply to imessage:+<redacted>\n\n\nSession state at time of issue (`agent:main:main` in sessions.json):\n\n{\n  \"deliveryContext\": {\n    \"channel\": \"imessage\",\n    \"to\": \"+<redacted>\",\n    \"accountId\": \"default\"\n  },\n  \"lastChannel\": \"imessage\",\n  \"lastTo\": \"+<redacted>\",\n  \"origin\": {\n    \"label\": \"openclaw-tui\",\n    \"provider\": \"imessage\",\n    \"surface\": \"webchat\",\n    \"chatType\": \"direct\",\n    \"to\": \"+<redacted>\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\n- **Affected:** Any user with iMessage configured who has ever used `openclaw tui --deliver`\n- **Severity:** High — unsolicited messages sent to personal phone number; user has no visible way to stop it from within the TUI\n- **Frequency:** 100% reproducible; persists indefinitely until manually patched\n- **Consequence:** Privacy concern (TUI conversations mirrored to SMS/iMessage); unexpected charges if carrier bills per message; user confusion\n\n### Additional information\n\n**Three issues identified — suggest fixing all three:**\n\n**1. `deliveryContext` not cleared when TUI reconnects without `--deliver`**\nThe gateway should clear or ignore stored `deliveryContext` when a TUI client connects without delivery mode. Delivery intent should be scoped to the active connection, not persisted indefinitely in session state.\n\n**2. Heartbeat with `target: \"last\"` should not mutate session `deliveryContext`**\nThe heartbeat fires every 30 min and re-writes iMessage delivery context onto the main session via `target: \"last\"`. This makes any manual cleanup of the session immediately undone. Heartbeat delivery should not update session routing state — consider storing heartbeat delivery separately or making `deliveryContext` immutable from the heartbeat path.\n\n**3. `/deliver off` TUI slash command forwarded to agent instead of handled locally**\nWhen the user typed `/deliver off` in the TUI, it was forwarded to the agent as a plain message rather than being intercepted by the TUI command handler. This left the user with no working UI mechanism to resolve the issue.\n\n**Workaround that resolved the issue:**\n```bash\nopenclaw config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.target none\n# Manually remove deliveryContext, lastChannel, lastTo, origin from agent:main:main in sessions.json\nopenclaw gateway restart\n```\n\n**Bonus: `imessage` not listed as valid heartbeat `target` option**\nDocs show `target: last | whatsapp | telegram | discord | none` — iMessage works implicitly via `last` but is not an explicit named option. Should be documented or added.","comments":[],"createdAt":"2026-03-05T06:35:55Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACQomLZw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACZxxN7g","name":"bug:behavior","description":"Incorrect behavior without a crash","color":"D73A4A"}],"number":35589,"title":"[Bug]: TUI responses delivered to iMessage when deliveryContext persists and heartbeat target is \"last\"","updatedAt":"2026-03-05T06:36:04Z","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/35589"},{"body":"### Bug type\n\nRegression (worked before, now fails)\n\n### Summary\n\nThe error \"Delivering to WhatsApp requires target <E.164|group JID>\" is incorrectly thrown when a user attempts to send an outbound WhatsApp message to a valid phone number that is not in the bot's allowFrom policy. Session may store `modelOverride` + `providerOverride` (or equivalent), but the UI that draws the checkmarks probably compares only the model id against the list.\n\n**Suggested fix:** When determining which list item is “current” for the session, compare using the full key `provider/modelId` (e.g. `nexus-d/claude-opus-4-6`), not just `modelId` (e.g. `claude-opus-4-6`). This causes Ollama to request 36GB of memory for a 2.5GB model, making it completely unusable on any machine with less than ~40GB RAM.\n\n## Error\n```\nmodel requires more system memory (34.4 GiB) than is available (17.7 GiB)\n```\n\n## Ollama runner log confirming hardcoded value\n```\nmsg=load request=\"{Operation:fit ... KvSize:262144 ...}\"\nmsg=\"kv cache\" device=CUDA0 size=\"36.0 GiB\"\nmsg=\"model weights\" device=CUDA0 size=\"2.3 GiB\"\nmsg=\"total memory\" size=\"39.5 GiB\"\n```\n\n## Config attempts that were all ignored\nAll of the following were tried and had zero effect:\n```json\n\"models.providers.ollama.models[].contextWindow\": 4096\n\"models.providers.ollama.models[].numCtx\": 4096\n\"models.providers.ollama.modelOptions.num_ctx\": 4096\n```\n```powershell\n$env:OLLAMA_MAX_NUM_CTX = \"4096\"\n```\nChanging api type from `openai-completions` to `ollama` — no effect.\n\n## Workaround (working)\nHTTP proxy on port 11435 that intercepts requests and rewrites num_ctx before forwarding to Ollama on 11434:\n```javascript\n// ollama-proxy.js\nconst http = require('http');\nconst PROXY_PORT = 11435;\nconst OLLAMA_PORT = 11434;\nconst MAX_CTX = 16000; // OpenClaw minimum is 16000\n\nconst server = http.createServer((req, res) => {\n  let body = '';\n  req.on('data', chunk => { body += chunk.toString(); });\n  req.on('end', () => {\n    let modifiedBody = body;\n    if (body && (req.headers['content-type'] || '').includes('application/json')) {\n      try {\n        const parsed = JSON.parse(body);\n        if (parsed.options && parsed.options.num_ctx) {\n          parsed.options.num_ctx = MAX_CTX;\n        } else {\n          if (!parsed.options) parsed.options = {};\n          parsed.options.num_ctx = MAX_CTX;\n        }\n        modifiedBody = JSON.stringify(parsed);\n      } catch (e) {}\n    }\n    const options = {\n      hostname: '127.0.0.1',\n      port: OLLAMA_PORT,\n      path: req.url,\n      method: req.method,\n      headers: { ...req.headers, 'host': `127.0.0.1:${OLLAMA_PORT}`, 'content-length': Buffer.byteLength(modifiedBody) }\n    };\n    const proxyReq = http.request(options, (proxyRes) => {\n      res.writeHead(proxyRes.statusCode, proxyRes.headers);\n      proxyRes.pipe(res, { end: true });\n    });\n    proxyReq.on('error', (err) => { res.writeHead(502); res.end('Proxy error: ' + err.message); });\n    proxyReq.write(modifiedBody);\n    proxyReq.end();\n  });\n});\n\nserver.listen(PROXY_PORT, '127.0.0.1', () => {\n  console.log(`Proxy running on ${PROXY_PORT}, forwarding to ${OLLAMA_PORT}`);\n});\n```\n\nThen set `baseUrl` in openclaw.json to point to the proxy:\n```json\n\"models\": {\n  \"providers\": {\n    \"ollama\": {\n      \"baseUrl\": \"http://localhost:11435\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Expected behavior\n`contextWindow` or an equivalent config key under `models.providers.ollama` should control the num_ctx sent to Ollama.\n\n## Impact\nThis bug makes OpenClaw completely unusable with Ollama on any normal consumer PC. The workaround requires running a separate proxy process on every startup, which is not acceptable for a production setup.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Switch back to Model A (198k).\n6. Configure multiple channels (webchat + feishu)\n2. Bind main agent to feishu channel via bindings config\n3. Webchat heartbeat polling sends a message with `from: \"heartbeat\"`, `provider: \"webchat\"`\n4. Main agent responds to the heartbeat message\n5. System incorrectly sets `deliveryContext.channel` to `\"feishu\"`\n6. Message delivery fails and enters delivery-queue for retry loop\n\n### Expected behavior\n\n1. Webchat heartbeat messages should NOT trigger cross-channel delivery\n2. The `heartbeat` placeholder should be recognized and skipped for delivery\n3. `deliveryContext.channel` should follow the message origin channel, not be overwritten by agent bindings\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nFeishu API returns error: `Invalid ids: [heartbeat]`. The message delivery fails and enters delivery-queue, causing retry loops on every gateway restart. Error log shows:\n```\ncode: 99992360\nmsg: The request you send is not a valid {user_id} or not exists\n```\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.1\n\n### Operating system\n\nWindows 11\n\n### Install method\n\nnpm global\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\nSession state in sessions.json shows:\n\n{\n  \"agent:main:main\": {\n    \"origin\": {\n      \"from\": \"heartbeat\",\n      \"to\": \"heartbeat\",\n      \"provider\": \"webchat\"\n    },\n    \"deliveryContext\": {\n      \"channel\": \"feishu\"  // Should be \"webchat\" or no delivery\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n\nDelivery queue entry:\n\n{\n  \"to\": \"heartbeat\",\n  \"accountId\": \"main\",\n  \"sessionKey\": \"agent:main:feishu:direct:heartbeat\",\n  \"text\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\nAffected: Users with multi-channel setup (webchat + feishu)\nSeverity: Medium (causes API errors and retry loops)\nFrequency: 100% repro when heartbeat triggers agent response\nConsequence: Gateway logs fill with errors, delivery-queue accumulates failed entries\n\n### Additional information\n\n**Root Cause:** The `deliveryContext` inheritance logic incorrectly uses the agent's channel binding instead of the message origin channel.\n\n**Workaround:** Disable or reduce heartbeat task frequency to avoid triggering this bug.\n\n**Suggested Fix:**\n1. Heartbeat messages (`from: \"heartbeat\"`) should be identified as system messages and not trigger message delivery\n2. `deliveryContext` should be derived from message origin (`provider` field), not from agent's channel bindings\n3. This threshold works for high-traffic channels (Slack/Discord) but iMessage can be legitimately quiet for hours. Result: 59 unnecessary provider restarts in 2 days, causing delivery gaps during active conversations. The restart cascade compounds — each restart resets the \"last event\" timer, so if no message arrives quickly after restart, the next 5-minute health check can flag it stale again almost immediately.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Configure OpenClaw with an iMessage channel on macOS.\n2. Leave the gateway running for any period with no inbound/outbound iMessage activity (30+ minutes).\n3. Check gateway.log — the iMessage provider will be restarted every ~30 minutes.\n4. Send a message during or immediately after a restart — delivery may be delayed.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe health monitor should not restart a provider that is functioning correctly just because the channel has been quiet. iMessage can go hours between messages without any socket problem. A per-channel configurable staleEventThresholdMs or provider-level keepalive pings would prevent false positives.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nThe iMessage provider is killed and restarted every ~30 minutes continuously, 24/7, regardless of actual socket health. During active conversations, these restarts cause transient delivery failures — outbound messages queue behind the restart cycle. Observed 59 stale-socket restarts in a 48-hour period. Restarts cascade: each restart resets the last-event timer, so subsequent 5-minute health checks can trigger another restart almost immediately.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\nv2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nmacOS 15.4 (Apple Silicon M4)\n\n### Install method\n\nnpm global\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\nSample from gateway.log showing continuous 30-minute restarts:\n\n\n2026-03-04T22:04:10.274Z [health-monitor] [imessage:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stale-socket)\n2026-03-04T22:29:10.287Z [health-monitor] [imessage:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stale-socket)\n2026-03-04T22:34:10.294Z [health-monitor] [imessage:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stale-socket)\n\n\nSource: DEFAULT_STALE_EVENT_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 * 6e4 in channel-health-monitor.ts\nNo per-channel config path exists — deps.timing?.staleEventThresholdMs is checked but never populated from openclaw.json.\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\nAffected: All iMessage channel users on always-on gateway deployments\nSeverity: High — blocks message delivery during active conversations\nFrequency: 100% repro — happens every 30 minutes on any idle iMessage channel\nConsequence: Missed/delayed message delivery, restart cascades during conversations, noisy logs (59 restarts in 48 hours obscure real issues)\n\n### Additional information\n\nProposed fix: (A) Make staleEventThresholdMs configurable per channel in openclaw.json, (B) Add iMessage-specific keepalive pings so idle sockets don't appear dead, or (C) both. This issue compounds with auto-compaction delivery blocking — when compaction runs during a stale-socket restart window, the user can wait 7+ minutes for a response that was already generated.","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87uiKgx","author":{"login":"SammyBuildsIt"},"authorAssociation":"NONE","body":"We hit this exact same pattern on Telegram with a 9-agent setup — 270+ false stale-socket restarts per day across our bots. To prevent an attacker from spoofing these markers using visually similar Unicode characters, the content is first passed through foldMarkerText, which maps certain Unicode homoglyphs to their ASCII equivalents (e.g., fullwidth < → <).\n\nHowever, the mapping table ANGLE_BRACKET_MAP currently covers only a subset of characters that can serve as substitutes for < and >. Many other Unicode characters that closely resemble angle brackets are missing, including guillemets, double angle brackets, and ornamental variants. An attacker could inject a marker like «EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT»; because it is not normalized, the subsequent regex (/<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT...>>>/gi) fails to detect it, leaving the spoofed marker untouched in the content. If the underlying LLM treats these Unicode characters as equivalent to < and > (e.g., through tokenization or Unicode normalization), the security boundary can be bypassed, potentially allowing the attacker to inject malicious instructions.\n\nThis is a follow-up for #30948 and 30951.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\nBecause this issue is reported publicly and I consider it a proactive hardening measure rather than an actively exploited vulnerability, I deliberately refrain from publishing exact exploit steps or proof‑of‑concept code. The goal is to raise the bar for potential adversaries while giving maintainers and advanced users enough information to understand the rationale behind the change.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe list should include these characters.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nThe list does not include these characters.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\nLatest\n\n### Operating system\n\nAll\n\n### Install method\n\n_No response_\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\n_No response_\n\n### Additional information\n\n_No response_","comments":[],"createdAt":"2026-03-04T20:01:20Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACQomLZw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACWBvIeA","name":"security","description":"Security documentation","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACZxxN7g","name":"bug:behavior","description":"Incorrect behavior without a crash","color":"D73A4A"}],"number":34943,"title":"[Security]: Potential security risk allowing the attacker to inject malicious instructions in src/security/external-contents.ts","updatedAt":"2026-03-04T20:03:36Z","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34943"},{"body":"### Bug type\n\nBehavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)\n\n### Summary\n\n With compaction.mode: \"safeguard\", OpenClaw calls the LLM API every ~30 minutes on all active sessions — including isolated cron sessions that contain no real conversation messages. Observe the response\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe agent should execute filesystem and system actions automatically using its available tools.\n\nFor example:\n- create hello.txt on the desktop\n- write files to disk\n- execute shell commands\n- deploy files to SSH hosts\n\nThis behavior was working normally before 4:00 AM ET.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nThe agent refuses to execute filesystem operations.\n\nInstead it returns instructions such as:\n- \"Run this in your terminal\"\n- \"Create this file manually\"\n\nExample message returned:\n\n\"Gateway running unreachable, but agent has no exec/read/write tools, only message and sessions. `commands.allowFrom` is evaluated later, setting `isAuthorizedSender=false` for unauthorized users\n3. `src/auto-reply/reply/command-gates.ts:7-17` - Command handlers return { shouldContinue: false } without a response message\n4. `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-inline-actions.ts:404-407` - The agent comes back up but sits idle — no continuation, no update to the user. Events from before the restart are not replayed. A new trigger is required every time to wake the agent.\nVersion: 2026.3.2 (85377a2)\nPlatform: Linux VPS\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\nStart a long-running or multi-step agent task (e.g. a cron job, a multi-tool workflow, or any task that takes more than ~30 seconds)\nWhile the task is in progress, trigger a gateway restart — via config.patch, health-monitor, watchdog, manual restart, or OS reboot\nWait for the gateway to come back up fully\nObserve that the agent is online but completely silent — no continuation of the task, no status update, no error message\nThe task only resumes if the user manually sends a new message\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nAfter a gateway restart, the agent should detect that a task was in progress and resume it automatically\nAt minimum, the agent should send a message to the user indicating the restart and the interrupted task\nAny events or messages generated before the restart that were not yet delivered should be flushed or re-queued on restart\nNo manual input from the user should be required\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nGateway restarts cleanly and reports healthy\nAgent is online and responsive but takes no action\nIn-flight task is silently dropped — no error, no notification, no partial result\nMessages generated by the agent before the restart that were not yet delivered are lost entirely\nThe agent waits indefinitely for a new user message before doing anything\nchannels status shows everything connected — no indication anything was lost\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nubuntu\n\n### Install method\n\n_No response_\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\n_No response_\n\n### Additional information\n\nWhat We've Tried (None Stable)\n\nApproach | Result\n-- | --\nBOOT.md with resume instructions | Agent reads it but takes no action without a trigger message\ngateway:start hook calling openclaw agent --message | Unstable — fires before gateway is fully ready, or fires multiple times in a restart storm causing duplicate wake events\n@reboot cron with openclaw agent --message | Only works on OS reboot, misses crash/config restarts\nSimulating user input via CLI on boot | Partially works but race conditions cause duplicate triggers or missed wakes\nHeartbeat cron every 15 min | Agent eventually wakes but with up to 15 min gap and no task context\n\nThe closest working solution is simulating user input on gateway:start, but it is not stable due to:\n\nNo deduplication across restart storms (each restart sends a new wake, even if a previous one is still processing)\nNo readiness guarantee (message fires before the agent channel is fully ready)\nNo task context passed with the wake event (agent knows to resume but not what to resume)\n\n\nRoot Cause (as understood)\n1. Events are not replayed after reconnect\nAfter a gateway restart, clients detect a sequence gap but events from before the disconnect are not replayed. Any messages or tool results generated during the interrupted turn are permanently lost.\n2. No persistent turn state\nThere is no mechanism to persist in-flight turn state (accumulated messages, tool call position, task context) to disk before a restart. When the process exits, all turn state is gone.\n3. No built-in post-restart trigger\nThe gateway has no native mechanism to automatically send a wake event or resume signal to agents after coming back up. BOOT.md is read passively — the agent only acts on it if something triggers a turn first.\n4. gateway:start hook fires too early\nThe gateway:start hook fires before all channels and agents are fully initialized. Persist turn state before shutdown\nBefore processing SIGUSR1 or exiting, flush any active turn's accumulated messages and state to disk (e.g. .openclaw/turn-state/). On next startup, restore and continue.\n2. Add a gateway:ready hook (fires after all channels initialized)\nA hook that fires only once all agents and channels are confirmed ready — not at process start. This would allow reliable post-restart wake messages without race conditions.\n3. Built-in resume event injection\nOn startup, if .openclaw/turn-state/ contains unfinished turns, automatically inject a system message into the relevant channel:\n[System] Gateway restarted. Task \"{task}\" was in progress. Resuming.\n4. Event replay or at-least-once delivery for turn messages\nMessages generated during a turn should be buffered until confirmed delivered. gateway (loopback:18789), LINE channel shows running/configured, but GET /line/webhook intermittently returns 404. LINE webhooks via ngrok then get 404 and no sessions are created. openclaw gateway restart immediately restores /line/webhook to 200.\n---\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n[ ] openclaw gateway restart\n[ ] sleep 2 && curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18789/line/webhook\n\n### Expected behavior\n\n/line/webhook should remain reachable while LINE channel is running.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nBody (copy/paste):\nVersion: OpenClaw 2026.3.2 (85377a2)\nOS: macOS (LaunchAgent service: ai.openclaw.gateway.plist)\nGateway: bind loopback, port 18789\nChannel: LINE plugin (line, accountId=default), running/configured=true\nSymptom: /line/webhook intermittently returns 404:\ncurl -i http://127.0.0.1:18789/line/webhook → 404 Not Found\nAt the same time, openclaw channels status --json shows line running/configured true (no lastError)\nopenclaw channels logs --channel line --lines 200 shows repeated [default] starting LINE provider (Steve hair) with no clear channel exited / auto-restart attempt\nWhen this happens, LINE webhooks via ngrok receive POST /line/webhook 404\nWorkaround: openclaw gateway restart immediately restores GET /line/webhook → 200 OK (and LINE works again)\nExpected: /line/webhook should remain reachable while LINE channel is running.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\nersion: OpenClaw 2026.3.2 (85377a2)\n\n### Operating system\n\nmacOS\n\n### Install method\n\n_No response_\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\n_No response_\n\n### Additional information\n\n_No response_","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87uVDqj","author":{"login":"joelnishanth"},"authorAssociation":"CONTRIBUTOR","body":"Working on this in #34646.\n\nRoot cause: `createGatewayPluginRequestHandler` pins the plugin registry at gateway startup. Set up OpenClaw with QQBot channel\n2. Have a conversation with the agent\n3. Observe that sometimes the agent doesn't respond immediately\n4. Send another message to trigger the pending response\n5. Also observe that multi-part replies sometimes get interrupted\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nAgent should respond immediately to each user message, and multi-part replies should complete without interruption.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\n(1) Agent doesn't respond to user message - no reply is sent until user sends another message. (2) Agent starts replying but stops mid-way - subsequent parts of the reply are not sent until user sends another message.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nUbuntu 24.04\n\n### Install method\n\nnpm global\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\nAffected: All users using messaging channels (QQBot, Telegram, etc.)\nSeverity: High (blocks normal conversation flow)\nFrequency: Intermittent but frequent\nConsequence: Users must send multiple messages to get a single response, degrading user experience significantly\n\nRoot cause analysis:\n1. In gateway.ts, if handleMessageFn throws an uncaught exception, messageProcessorRunning stays true, blocking subsequent messages\n2. In reply-DhtejUNZ.js, after timeout, aborted=true causes subsequent enqueue calls to silently drop messages\n3. Dispatcher's pending counter has race conditions that may trigger premature onIdle or incomplete state cleanup\n\n### Additional information\n\nRelated to issue #34156 (XML tags leakage). Three layers of missing implementation: no mention gating in the inbound flow, no pending history support, and LINE missing from the DOCKS registry.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n1. Configure a LINE channel account with a group entry and set `requireMention: true`.\n2. Add the bot to a LINE group.\n3. Send a message in the group **without** mentioning the bot.\n4. Observe that the bot processes and replies to the message.\n\n### Expected behavior\nWhen `requireMention: true` is set, unmentioned group messages should be stored as conversation context (pending history) but **not** trigger a reply. Only messages where the bot is explicitly mentioned should produce a response. This is how WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, and iMessage all behave.\n\n### Actual behavior\nThe bot processes and responds to every group message regardless of whether it was mentioned. The `requireMention` setting has no observable effect.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.2.26\n\n### Operating system\n\nDebian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), kernel 6.8.0-51-generic (x86_64)\n\n### Install method\n\ndocker\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n#### Root cause analysis\n\nThree layers of missing implementation:\n\n**1. No mention gating in the LINE inbound flow**\n\n`requireMention` is defined in `src/line/types.ts` and `src/line/config-schema.ts` but is never read or applied anywhere. `handleMessageEvent` calls `processMessage` unconditionally after sender authorization:\n\n```\nhandleLineWebhookEvents\n  └─ handleMessageEvent\n       ├─ shouldProcessLineEvent   // sender authorization only — no mention check\n       ├─ downloadLineMedia\n       ├─ buildLineMessageContext\n       └─ processMessage           // ⚠️ called unconditionally — no mention gating\n```\n\nAll other channels gate on mentions before dispatching: Discord and Slack use `resolveMentionGatingWithBypass` in the handler layer; Telegram uses it in the context builder layer; WhatsApp uses `applyGroupGating()`.\n\n**2. No pending history support**\n\nEvery other channel uses `recordPendingHistoryEntryIfEnabled` (`src/auto-reply/reply/history.ts`) to store unmentioned group messages as context. LINE has no equivalent:\n\n| Channel | Pending history location |\n|---------|------------------------|\n| WhatsApp | `web/auto-reply/monitor/group-gating.ts` |\n| Telegram | `telegram/bot-message-context.ts` |\n| Discord | `discord/monitor/message-handler.preflight.ts` |\n| Slack | `slack/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts` |\n| Signal | `signal/monitor/event-handler.ts` |\n| iMessage | `imessage/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` |\n| **LINE** | **❌ missing** |\n\nWithout pending history, any mention gating fix that blocks at inbound will cause context gaps — the agent loses all unmentioned group conversation when it is later mentioned.\n\n**3. LINE missing from DOCKS registry (`src/channels/dock.ts`)**\n\nThe `DOCKS` object registers `resolveRequireMention` for 8 channels — LINE is absent. The reply-stage shared lookup `resolveGroupRequireMention` (`src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts`) falls back to `return true` for LINE. LINE's reply flow does reach this path:\n\n```\ndispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher\n  → getReplyFromConfig → session.ts → resolveReplyDirectives\n  → resolveGroupRequireMention → getChannelDock(\"line\")   // undefined → fallback\n```\n\nAdditionally, `CHAT_CHANNEL_ORDER` in `src/channels/registry.ts` does not include `\"line\"`, so adding LINE to DOCKS also requires updating this array (otherwise `ChatChannelId` type will not include `\"line\"`).\n\nConfirmed on both the local build and the current `main` branch (as of 2026-03-04).\n\n### Impact and severity\n\n- **Affected:** All LINE users who configure `requireMention: true` on group/room channels\n- **Severity:** High — a documented configuration option is silently ignored, leading to unintended bot responses in group chats\n- **Frequency:** 100% reproducible — the code path simply does not exist\n- **Consequence:** Bot replies to all group messages, causing noise and potentially unexpected API usage costs\n\n### Additional information\n\n#### On the correct gating layer\n\nMention gating must not simply block the message at inbound (dropping it entirely), nor should it only gate at reply time (after the agent has already run inference):\n\n- **Inbound-only block** → unmentioned messages never enter the session. When the bot is later mentioned, it has no memory of the preceding conversation — context gaps degrade agent quality.\n- **Reply-only gate** → the agent runs full inference and possibly executes tool calls, then the reply is suppressed. Wastes tokens and risks side effects.\n\nThe correct behavior — consistent with WhatsApp's `applyGroupGating()` — is:\n\n> **Store unmentioned messages as conversation context (pending history), but do not trigger a reply.**\n\n### Related Issues\n\n- #16975 — LINE plugin: group mention gating has no effect\n- #29746 — LINE plugin: group requireMention / mentionPatterns not enforced\n- #29786 (PR, open) — partial fix: adds mention gating in `shouldProcessLineEvent`, but does not add pending history, does not register LINE in DOCKS, and places content gating in the access control Start a session with the Kimi model\n2. Make several tool calls (read, write, exec)\n3. After some time or after certain operations (memory compaction), subsequent tool calls fail with \"Tool not found\"\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nTool calls should work consistently regardless of the toolCallId format.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nTool calls fail with \"Tool not found\" when the toolCallId has inconsistent formatting.\n### Observed toolCallId formats and results:\n\n| toolCallId Format | Result |\n|-------------------|--------|\n| `functions.read:0` | ✅ Works |\n| `functions.write:1` | ✅ Works |\n| `functions.exec:2` | ✅ Works |\n| `functions.read1` | ❌ Tool not found |\n| `functionsread3` | ❌ Tool not found |\n| `functionswrite4` | ❌ Tool not found |\n\n## Root Cause\nThe gateway's tool router cannot handle inconsistent toolCallId formats. It expects a specific format (with `.` separator and `:` index) but the Kimi model sometimes generates toolCallIds without the proper separator.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nUbuntu 24.04.4 LTS (GNU/Linux 6.8.0-101-generic x86_64)\n\n### Install method\n\nStandard shell script\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n{\"type\":\"message\",\"id\":\"...\",\"message\":{\"role\":\"toolResult\",\"toolCallId\":\"functionsread3\",\"toolName\":\"unknown\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Tool  not found\"}],\"isError\":true}}\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\nAffected: all sessions\nSeverity: High; replies are being blocked\nFrequency: 90%\nConsequence: agents cannot respond\n\n### Additional information\n\n## Workaround\nStart a new session using `/new` in chat or `openclaw agent --agent main` via CLI.\n\n## Suggested Fix\nNormalize toolCallId parsing in the gateway to handle multiple formats:\n- `functions.read:0` (Anthropic format)\n- `functions.read0` (missing colon)\n- `functionsread0` (missing separator entirely)\n\nExtract the tool name consistently by removing the  Agents running in Sandbox environment cannot load OpenClaw's pre-installed default skills( such as: `skill-creator`), and encounter \"Path escapes sandbox root\" error when attempting to read skill files.\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n  1. 在 OpenClaw 中启用 sandbox 模式（sandbox.mode = \"all\"）\n  Enable sandbox mode in OpenClaw (sandbox.mode = \"all\")\n  2. 配置 agent 使用默认的 workspace 路径\n  Configure agent to use default workspace path\n  3. 触发需要使用预装 skills 的场景（例如调用 /skill-creator 或其他内置技能）\n  Trigger scenarios requiring bundled skills (e.g., invoke /skill-creator or other built-in skills)\n  4. Agent 尝试读取技能文件 SKILL.md\n  Agent attempts to read skill file SKILL.md\n  5. 出现错误：\"[tools] read failed: Path escapes sandbox root (~/.openclaw/workspace): /home/user/.nvm/versions/node/vX.X.X/lib/node_modules/openclaw/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md\"\n  Error occurs: \"[tools] read failed: Path escapes sandbox root (~/.openclaw/workspace): /home/user/.nvm/versions/node/vX.X.X/lib/node_modules/openclaw/skills/skill-name/SKILL.md\"\n\n\n### Expected behavior\n\n-   Agent 应该能够正常访问和读取预装的 skills 文件，就像在非 sandbox 环境中一样。\n-   Agent should be able to normally access and read bundled skills files, just like in non-sandbox environments.\n\n\n### Actual behavior\n\n-   Agent 无法读取预装 skills 文件，工具调用失败并返回路径逃逸错误。只有 workspace 目录下的自定义 skills 可以正常工作。\n-   Agent cannot read bundled skills files, tool calls fail with path escape error. Configure multiple subagents (builder, reviewer) in openclaw.json\n2. Spawn multiple subagents using sessions_spawn\n3. Wait for subagent completion events\n4. Observe the output message in user-facing channels (e.g., QQ bot)\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nClean user-facing output without any XML tags or template delimiters visible.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nOutput contains raw XML tags and template delimiters:\n- </arg_value></tool_call>\n- <|assistant|>---\n\nThis is a systemic stream contamination issue affecting multiple output formats.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nLinux Ubuntu 24.04\n\n### Install method\n\nnpm global\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\nAffected: All users using subagent spawns\nSeverity: Medium (visual pollution, confusing UX)\nFrequency: Intermittent (occurs during subagent completion events)\nConsequence: Users see raw XML/template markers in output, degrading trust in the system\n\n### Additional information\n\nRoot cause hypothesis:\n1. XmlStreamWriter flushes before content is complete\n2. Subagent streaming output is piped directly to main output without isolation\n3. Race condition between XML encapsulation and streaming transmission\n4. Prompt template boundaries not properly stripped before user output\n\nThis affects both XML tags (</arg_value>, </tool_call>) and template delimiters (<|assistant|>), indicating a systemic issue in the output stream pipeline.","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87uMRsu","author":{"login":"openperf"},"authorAssociation":"CONTRIBUTOR","body":"This issue has been addressed in PR #34168.\n\n**Root Cause**\n\nThe sanitization pipeline (`sanitizeTextContent` / `extractAssistantText`) only handled Minimax-specific XML and thinking tags, but missed two other common artifact types leaked from subagent streams:\n\n1. **Generic tool call XML** — Models like Qwen and Ollama emit `<tool_call>`, `<arg_name>`, `<arg_value>` tags. When streaming is interrupted, stray tags like `</arg_value></tool_call>` leak into user-facing text.\n2. **ChatML delimiters** — ChatML-format models can leak `<|assistant|>---`, `<|im_start|>assistant\\n`, `<|im_end|>`, etc.\n\n**Fix**\n\nPR #34168 adds two new sanitizer functions to the pipeline:\n\n- `stripGenericToolCallXml` — removes full `<tool_call>…</tool_call>` blocks and orphaned opening/closing tags.\n- `stripChatMlDelimiters` — strips all known ChatML delimiters, including the two-part `<|im_start|>role` token with its trailing role word.\n\nBoth are integrated into `sanitizeTextContent` (sessions-helpers.ts) and `extractAssistantText` (pi-embedded-utils.ts), with comprehensive unit tests covering all Setup: 4 agents, 4 Telegram bots, 4 Discord bots, 1 Slack bot on 7.6GB RAM VPS.","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87uKW8a","author":{"login":"mdlmarkham"},"authorAssociation":"NONE","body":"## 🔧 Hephaestus Code Review Analysis\n\n### Root Cause Identified\n\nThe stale-socket detection logic in `channel-health-monitor.ts` has an edge case that causes false positives in multi-account/low-traffic scenarios.\n\n**The problematic code:**\n```typescript\n// Line 62-72 in isChannelHealthy()\nif (snapshot.lastEventAt != null || snapshot.lastStartAt != null) {\n  const upSince = snapshot.lastStartAt ?? 0;\n  const upDuration = opts.now - upSince;\n  if (upDuration > opts.staleEventThresholdMs) {\n    const lastEvent = snapshot.lastEventAt ?? 0;  // <-- BUG: treats null as epoch\n    const eventAge = opts.now - lastEvent;\n    if (eventAge > opts.staleEventThresholdMs) {\n      return false;  // <-- Marks as unhealthy\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**The issue:**\n- If `lastEventAt` is `null` (channel never received an event), then `lastEvent = 0`\n- `eventAge = now - 0` = current timestamp (definitely > 30 min threshold)\n- Any channel running >30 min with no events gets marked as `stale-socket`\n\n**Why this happens in multi-account setups:**\n1. All 9 channels start around the same time\n2. Low-traffic channels (Telegram bots, Slack with quiet servers) may not receive events for hours\n3. After 30 min of no events, health monitor restarts them\n4. Restart creates new socket, but if still no traffic → cycle repeats\n\n**Existing test confirms this is intentional behavior:**\n```typescript\n// channel-health-monitor.test.ts:235\nit(\"restarts a channel that never received any event past the stale threshold\", async () => {\n  // ... expects restart when lastEventAt is undefined\n});\n```\n\n### Suggested Fixes\n\n**Option A: Require prior event before stale detection**\nOnly treat as stale if we've seen at least one event:\n```typescript\nif (upDuration > opts.staleEventThresholdMs) {\n  // Only consider stale if we've seen events before\n  if (snapshot.lastEventAt == null) {\n    return true;  // Never received event = can't determine staleness\n  }\n  const eventAge = opts.now - snapshot.lastEventAt;\n  if (eventAge > opts.staleEventThresholdMs) {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Option B: Channel-type-specific thresholds**\nTelegram polling has different traffic patterns than Slack WebSocket.\n\n**Option C: Configurable disable**\nAdd `disableStaleDetection: true` option per channel or globally.\n\n**Option D: Use lastSuccessfulPoll/heartbeat**\nInstead of just `lastEventAt`, track successful connection health.\n\n### Workaround (Immediate)\n\nSet a very high stale threshold in gateway config:\n```yaml\nhealthCheck:\n  staleEventThresholdMs: 86400000  # 24 hours\n\\}```\n\nOr disable health check entirely (not recommended):\n```yaml\nhealthCheck:\n  disabled: true\n```\n\n---\n\nWould be happy to submit a PR for Option A if the maintainers agree with the approach. But because the config reference is stale, runtime changes (e.g. toggling `requireMention`, changing group policy, updating allowlists) are silently ignored.\n\nNotably, `resolveAgentRoute` in the same file already calls `loadConfig()` per-message (line 68), confirming this is the intended pattern — the other 4 call sites just weren't updated to match.\n\n### Additional issues found\n\nThe group policy resolution functions (`resolveGroupPolicyFor`, `resolveGroupRequireMentionFor`, `resolveGroupActivationFor`) don't thread `accountId`, so non-default WhatsApp accounts lose their per-account group policy, allowlists, and mention settings when reading fresh config.\n\n`hasGroupAllowFrom` is also only computed from top-level `cfg.channels.whatsapp`, ignoring account-specific overrides — accounts with `groupAllowFrom` set only at account level get `false`, causing valid messages to be dropped under `groupPolicy: \"allowlist\"`.\n\n### Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Run OpenClaw v2026.3.3 with a configured Telegram bot.\n2. Ensure the bot is a member of a Telegram Supergroup with Topics enabled.\n3. Engage in a multi-turn conversation with an agent in a topic, particularly one involving tool use.\n4. Observe that some agent replies are not delivered to the Telegram client.\n5. Check the session history in the OpenClaw Web UI to confirm that the agent did generate a response that was not delivered.\n\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nAll agent replies generated by the gateway should be delivered as messages to the corresponding Telegram topic.\n\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nSome agent replies are silently dropped. The gateway logs may show a \"telegram sendMessage ok\" status, but the message does not arrive in the Telegram client. The user is unaware a reply was sent unless they check the Web UI.\n\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.3\n\n### Operating system\n\nmacOS 26.2\n\n### Install method\n\npnpm dev\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\nThe issue is a silent failure. SELinux denying the container read access to config files\n2. UID mismatch between the host `openclaw` user and the container's `node` user\n3. Podman being unable to read the `EnvironmentFile` after ownership is corrected for the container process\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Run `setup-podman.sh --quadlet` on Fedora Silverblue\n2. Start the service: `sudo systemctl --machine openclaw@ --user start openclaw.service`\n3. Service enters `auto-restart-queued` loop and never becomes active\n\n## Issue 1: SELinux Denials\n\nThe config directory `~openclaw/.openclaw/` is created with the `user_home_t` SELinux label. Containers run with the `container_t` context and SELinux (enforcing by default on Fedora) denies read access.\n\n**AVC denial example:**\n```\navc: denied { read } for comm=\"openclaw-gatewa\" name=\"openclaw.json\"\nscontext=system_u:system_r:container_t:s0\ntcontext=unconfined_u:object_r:user_home_t:s0\n```\n\n**Workaround:** Manually relabel the directory:\n```bash\nsudo chcon -Rt container_file_t /var/home/openclaw/.openclaw\n```\n\n**Proper fix:** Add `:Z` to the volume mount in the generated Quadlet file so Podman handles relabeling automatically:\n```\nVolume=/var/home/openclaw/.openclaw:/home/node/.openclaw:Z\n```\n\n## Issue 2: UID Mismatch with --userns=keep-id\n\nThe generated Quadlet file uses `UserNS=keep-id` and `User=%U:%G`. On Fedora Silverblue, the `openclaw` host user is assigned uid **1001**, but the `node` user inside the container is uid **1000**.\n\nWith `--userns=keep-id`, the container process runs as the host uid (1001), which appears as `openclaw` inside the container rather than `node`. This creates a flickering effect where messages appear twice, then one is removed.\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Configure OpenClaw with `channels.telegram.streaming: \"partial\"` (this is the default in some configurations)\n2. Send messages via Telegram to the bot\n3. Observe that each message appears twice in the Telegram client\n4. After a brief delay (1-3 seconds), one duplicate is automatically deleted\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\nMessages should appear once without duplication, regardless of streaming mode.\n\n## Actual Behavior\n\n- Each message renders twice in the Telegram client\n- One duplicate is auto-deleted by Telegram after arriving\n- Creates visual flicker and confusion\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\n\nThe partial streaming mode sends message chunks that Telegram renders as separate messages. When the complete message arrives, Telegram's deduplication logic removes what it perceives as a duplicate.\n\n## Temporary Workaround\n\nSet `channels.telegram.streaming` to `\"off\"` in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"channels\": {\n    \"telegram\": {\n      \"streaming\": \"off\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThen restart the gateway:\n```bash\nopenclaw gateway restart\n```\n\n### Workaround Trade-offs\n- **Pros:** Eliminates duplicate message display\n- **Cons:** Loses the streaming text / typing indicator effect in Telegram\n\n## Suggested Permanent Fix\n\nThe Telegram channel plugin should either:\n1. Use proper message editing for streaming updates (send once, edit in place)\n2. Implement proper deduplication tokens to prevent Telegram from treating chunks as separate messages\n3. Disable partial streaming by default for Telegram until the issue is resolved\n\n## Environment\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| OpenClaw Version | 2026.3.2 |\n| OS | macOS 26.3 (arm64) |\n| Node | v25.6.1 |\n| Channel | Telegram |\n| Date Discovered | 2026-03-03 |\n\n## Additional Context\n\nThis issue affects the user experience significantly in 1:1 chats but not group conversations. Every model we tested (across multiple providers) consistently reports that it has no file-writing tools available. The onboarding chat appears to work — the LLM claims files were created and bootstrap files removed but nothing is actually persisted to disk.\n\nWe traced the root cause to openclaw.json containing \"tools\": { \"profile\": \"messaging\" } after non-interactive onboard completes. This profile appears to restrict the agent to messaging-only tools, stripping all filesystem and shell access. By contrast, the interactive openclaw configure command does not set this field, leaving agents with the full default toolset and everything works as expected.\n\nOur workaround is to patch \"tools\": {} in the config after onboarding.\n\nWas the tools.profile = \"messaging\" default for openclaw onboard introduced recently (around 2026.3.2)? If so, is the team aware that this effectively breaks the core onboarding flow (at least it does here)? Agents that can't touch the filesystem can't do much of anything beyond chat. When asking it just says \" I don't have any file-writing tools available.\"\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe bootstrap process finalizes as it always did.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nNo files changed, bootstrap never finished, agent doesnt work as it doesnt have an identity\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2\n\n### Operating system\n\nDebian 12\n\n### Install method\n\ninstall script, is npm I believe\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\nHighly severe as if this happens, nothing really works - very frustrating\n\n\n### Additional information\n\nWhen 2026.3.1 created a config, it didn't put the tools section in there.","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87t8fEc","author":{"login":"qiaozhi-4"},"authorAssociation":"NONE","body":"I also encountered this problem. GPU","updatedAt":"2026-03-05T12:25:10Z","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33163"},{"body":"### Bug type\n\nBehavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)\n\n### Summary\n\nAfter a clean installation and onboarding, visiting http://127.0.0.1:18789/ immediately redirects to /chat?session=main and shows unauthorized: gateway token missing. The gateway logs confirm token_missing. However, manual WebSocket test with websocat using the same token succeeds, proving the gateway and token are functional.\n\n\n\n### Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Install OpenClaw on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 server using the official script:\n`curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`\n\n2. Run `openclaw onboard --install-daemon` and choose QuickStart (skip model config if desired).\n\n3. On the server, confirm the gateway is listening:\n`sudo systemctl status openclaw-gateway` → active, and `curl http://127.0.0.1:18789` returns HTML.\n\n4. Get the token from` ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.\n\n5. From a Mac, establish an SSH tunnel:\n`ssh -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 ubuntu@<server-ip>`\n\n6. In a Chrome/Chromium incognito window, visit `http://127.0.0.1:18789/`.\n\n### Expected behavior\n\nThe browser should display a login page (likely at /login) where the user can paste the token. After entering a valid token, the WebSocket connection should succeed and the chat interface should load.\n\n### Actual behavior\n\nThe page immediately redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:18789/chat?session=main` and shows:\n\n- unauthorized: gateway token missing (open the dashboard URL and paste the token in Control UI settings) - \n\nThe gateway logs repeatedly show `reason=token_missing` for WebSocket connections from `127.0.0.1`. Browser Developer Tools → Network tab confirms the WebSocket upgrade request to `ws://127.0.0.1:18789/` does not include the `?access_token=` parameter.\n\n### OpenClaw version\n\n2026.3.2 (85377a2) – confirmed via openclaw --version\n\n### Operating system\n\nServer: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) Client: macOS (tested on Sonoma) with Chrome 145 and Safari 26\n\n### Install method\n\nOfficial installer script: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash\n\n### Logs, screenshots, and evidence\n\n```shell\n- Server-side WebSocket test (succeeds):\n \"ws://127.0.0.1:18789/?access_token=abc123def456\"\n→ Returns\n{\"type\":\"event\",\"event\":\"connect.challenge\",\"payload\":{\"nonce\":\"...\",\"ts\":...}}\n- Browser Network tab evidence:\nThe WebSocket connection request (type `websocket`) shows no query parameters.\n- Gateway logs:\n\n[ws] closed before connect ... reason=unauthorized: gateway token missing\n```\n\n### Impact and severity\n\nAffected users: Any user trying to access the Web UI via SSH tunnel (or presumably any localhost access).\n\nSeverity: Blocks workflow – users cannot log in to the Web UI at all, despite a functioning backend.\n\nFrequency: Always – reproducible on every fresh install.\n\nConsequence: Users are forced to use the TUI (openclaw tui) exclusively; the Web UI is unusable.\n\n### Additional information\n\nThe token is valid (proven by websocat).\n\nClearing all browser storage (LocalStorage, SessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cookies, Cache) in incognito mode does not resolve the issue.\n\nDirectly visiting /login still redirects to /chat.\n\nThe same behavior occurs in Safari (private window) and Chrome (incognito).\n\nThis happens on a completely fresh Ubuntu 24.04 installation with no prior OpenClaw config.\n\nSuspect: Frontend routing bug – the login page is skipped because the app believes the user is already authenticated (perhaps reading an empty token from storage or an incorrect state).\n\n","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87t8-9X","author":{"login":"jaredbarranco"},"authorAssociation":"NONE","body":"Sorry if the meta commentary is not welcome here ... but I spent probably 3 hours last night trying to get Openclaw setup on a small ubuntu node inside my network... This bug is a nasty one because there is no prompt for any authentication when accessing the control-ui/browser dashboard.","createdAt":"2026-03-03T16:30:44Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33157#issuecomment-3992186711","viewerDidAuthor":false},{"id":"IC_kwDOQb6kR87t9Fyg","author":{"login":"newcodebook"},"authorAssociation":"NONE","body":"You’re not doing anything wrong — the Control UI token is **not** passed as a `?access_token=` query param anymore. `openclaw dashboard` intentionally puts it in the **URL fragment** (`#token=...`) so it doesn’t leak via logs/referrers.\n\nQuick workaround (works well over SSH tunnels):\n\n1) On the server, run:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw dashboard --no-open\n```\n\n2) Copy the printed URL and open it locally through your tunnel *exactly as-is* (including the `#token=...` fragment). The UI should read the fragment and persist it, then the WS connect will authenticate.\n\nIf it still redirects to `/chat` and drops the fragment, try explicitly loading the root with the fragment:\n\n- `http://127.0.0.1:18789/#token=<YOUR_TOKEN>`\n\nRefs (CoClaw):\n- https://coclaw.com/guides/control-ui-auth-and-pairing\n- https://coclaw.com/troubleshooting/solutions/control-ui-unauthorized\n\nIf you can paste one WS request line from DevTools (the full URL it tries to connect to) + your `gateway.controlUi.basePath` (if set), that’ll help confirm whether this is a frontend redirect bug vs a basePath/routing mismatch.\n","createdAt":"2026-03-03T16:35:34Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33157#issuecomment-3992214688","viewerDidAuthor":false}],"createdAt":"2026-03-03T15:14:52Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACQomLZw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDOQb6kR88AAAACZxxN7g","name":"bug:behavior","description":"Incorrect behavior without a crash","color":"D73A4A"}],"number":33157,"title":"[Bug]: Web UI redirects to /chat with \"token missing\" despite valid token – backend WebSocket works","updatedAt":"2026-03-03T16:35:34Z","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33157"}]

No — `job.sessionKey` was already set by the cron tool from the agent's own session context; it is only echoed back to the same webhook endpoint the job owner configured.\n\n## Repro + Verification\n\n### Environment\n\n- OS: macOS\n- Runtime/container: Node 22\n- Integration/channel: OpenAI-compatible API → cron tool\n\n### Steps\n\n1. Yes — additive fields only, omitted when undefined\n- Config/env changes? No\n- Migration needed? No\n\n## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)\n\n- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert the `enrichedPayload` block in `server-cron.ts` and restore `payload: evt`\n- Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/server-cron.ts`\n- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: webhook receivers that do strict schema validation and reject unknown fields\n\n## Risks and Mitigations\n\n- Risk: Webhook receivers with strict JSON schema validation may reject the additional fields.\n  - Mitigation: Both fields are additive and only present when non-empty; receivers should tolerate unknown fields per standard REST practice.\n\nMade with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)","number":37144,"title":"Cron: enrich webhook finished-event payload with jobName and callerSessionKey","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/37144"},{"body":"## Summary\n\n- Resolve relative `MEDIA:` paths (e.g., `MEDIA:./image.png`) against configured allowed media roots instead of the gateway process CWD, making local file delivery deterministic.\n- Correct misleading prompt guidance that claimed absolute and `~` paths are always blocked.\n\nCloses #37111\n\n## Root Cause\n\nIn `src/web/media.ts`, when a relative path reaches `assertLocalMediaAllowed`, it falls through to `path.resolve(mediaPath)` (line 94) which resolves against `process.cwd()`. If the path has leading/trailing whitespace, the URL check passes correctly, but all subsequent operations receive a path that doesn't exist on disk.\n\n**Impact:** Voice message conversion silently fails when file paths have surrounding whitespace — ffprobe/ffmpeg receive `\"  /path/to/file.ogg  \"` instead of `\"/path/to/file.ogg\"`, causing \"No such file\" errors.\n\n## Change type\n\nBug fix — use the trimmed path consistently throughout the function.\n\n## Changes\n\n- **`src/discord/voice-message.ts`**\n  - Replace 4 remaining uses of `filePath` with `trimmed` (after the existing `filePath.trim()` on line 151):\n    - `path.extname(trimmed)` instead of `path.extname(filePath)`\n    - `runFfprobe([..., trimmed])` instead of `runFfprobe([..., filePath])`\n    - `return { path: trimmed, ... }` instead of `return { path: filePath, ... }`\n    - `runFfmpeg([..., \"-i\", trimmed, ...])` instead of `runFfmpeg([..., \"-i\", filePath, ...])`\n\n- **`src/discord/voice-message.test.ts`**\n  - Add 3 new test cases:\n    - URL rejection works with surrounding whitespace\n    - Trimmed path is passed to ffprobe (not the original)\n    - Trimmed path is passed to ffmpeg (not the original)\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] All 7 tests pass (4 existing + 3 new)\n- [x] Linter passes with 0 warnings\n\n## Security\n\nStrengthens path validation — ensures the trimmed path used for URL rejection is the same path passed to subprocess commands, preventing any bypass via whitespace padding.\n\n## Compatibility\n\nFully backward-compatible. A bot named `@mybot` incorrectly triggers on text containing `@mybothelper`, `@mybot_v2`, or any other username that starts with the bot's username.\n\n**Impact:** The bot responds to messages that mention a *different* user whose username happens to start with the bot's username. This affects `requireMention` gating and ACK reactions — the bot processes messages it shouldn't.\n\n## Change type\n\nBug fix — replace `includes()` with an `indexOf` loop that verifies the character after the matched `@username` is not a valid Telegram username character (`[a-z0-9_]`).\n\n## Changes\n\n- **`src/telegram/bot/helpers.ts`**\n  - Add `TELEGRAM_USERNAME_CHAR` regex constant\n  - Replace `text.includes(...)` with a loop that checks all occurrences and validates the following character is not a valid username character (word boundary)\n  - The entity-based fallback (lines 288–297) already uses exact comparison (`===`) and is unaffected\n\n- **`src/telegram/bot/helpers.test.ts`**\n  - Add 10 new test cases for `hasBotMention` covering:\n    - Exact mention at end of text\n    - Mention followed by punctuation / space\n    - **Substring false-positive prevention** (prefix, underscore, digit suffixes)\n    - Entity-based detection for different users\n    - Caption-based messages\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n```ts\nimport { hasBotMention } from \"./helpers.js\";\n\n// Before fix: true (BUG — @mybothelper is a different user)\nhasBotMention({ text: \"hello @mybothelper\" }, \"mybot\");\n\n// After fix: false (correct — only exact @mybot matches)\nhasBotMention({ text: \"hello @mybothelper\" }, \"mybot\");\n\n// Still works for exact mentions:\nhasBotMention({ text: \"hello @mybot\" }, \"mybot\");        // true\nhasBotMention({ text: \"hello @mybot!\" }, \"mybot\");       // true\nhasBotMention({ text: \"@mybot how are you\" }, \"mybot\");  // true\n```\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] All 10 new `hasBotMention` tests pass\n- [x] All 49 tests in `helpers.test.ts` pass (39 existing + 10 new)\n- [x] Linter passes with 0 warnings\n\n## Security\n\nNo security impact.
