This prevented prompt cache hits, causing all 158k tokens to be charged as new input on every turn.\n\n## Change\n\nRemoved from `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts`:\n- `timestamp: timestampStr` field from conversationInfo object\n- Unused formatConversationTimestamp() function\n- Unused formatZonedTimestamp import\n\nThread context still includes thread_label and other static identifiers.\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [ ] Start Discord thread conversation\n- [ ] Send multiple messages\n- [ ] Verify prompt cache accumulates (check API response cache_creation_input_tokens in first message, then cache_read_input_tokens in subsequent messages)\n- [ ] Verify no timestamp field in injected context\n\nFixes #37047","number":37093,"title":"fix(context): remove timestamp from conversation metadata for prompt cache","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/37093"},{"body":"Fix broken cross-doc anchor in the Xfinity/Comcast SSL FAQ entry.\n\nCloses #36970","number":37092,"title":"docs(faq): fix broken troubleshooting anchor for Xfinity SSL note","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/37092"},{"body":"## Summary\n\n- Add `\"matrix\"` to `VOICE_BUBBLE_CHANNELS` in `src/tts/tts.ts` so TTS auto-replies on Matrix use Opus format with `voiceCompatible: true`, enabling native MSC3245 voice message bubbles instead of generic audio file attachments.\n\n## Root Cause\n\nThe `VOICE_BUBBLE_CHANNELS` set included `telegram`, `feishu`, and `whatsapp` but was missing `matrix`. wrap `rest.delete` with `request()`\n  - `removeOwnReactionsDiscord`: destructure `request`; wrap the initial `rest.get` (fetch message) and each `rest.delete` (remove reaction) with `request()`\n  - `fetchReactionsDiscord`: destructure `request`; wrap both `rest.get` calls (fetch message + fetch reaction users) with `request()`\n\n- **`src/discord/send.reactions.test.ts`** — New test file with 6 test cases covering all four reaction functions\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n```ts\n// Before fix: removeReactionDiscord bypasses retry\nconst { rest } = createDiscordClient(opts, cfg);\nawait rest.delete(...); // 429 → immediate failure, no retry\n\n// After fix: uses request() for retry\nconst { rest, request } = createDiscordClient(opts, cfg);\nawait request(() => rest.delete(...), \"unreact\"); // 429 → retried\n```\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] All 6 new unit tests pass\n- [x] Existing test suite unaffected\n- [x] Linter passes with 0 warnings\n\n## Security\n\nNo security impact. This change only adds retry wrapping around existing REST calls.\n\n## Compatibility\n\nFully backward-compatible. The retry runner is already created by `createDiscordClient` but was not being used by these functions.\n\n\nMade with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)","number":37084,"title":"fix(discord): wrap reaction REST calls with retry runner for consistency","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/37084"},{"body":"## Summary\n\n- Matrix TTS replies were sent as generic audio file attachments\n- Missing from VOICE_BUBBLE_CHANNELS set in src/tts/tts.ts\n- Enables native MSC3245 voice bubble support\n\n## Impact\n\nMatrix users configured with `messages.tts.auto: \"inbound\"` will now receive TTS replies as native voice message bubbles with:\n- Waveform visualization\n- Duration display\n- Inline playback controls\n\nThis improves user experience for ~1500+ active Matrix users in the open-source community.\n\n## Root Cause\n\nMatrix channel was missing from VOICE_BUBBLE_CHANNELS, causing resolveOutputFormat() to skip voice-compatible settings. gateway timeout or transient network errors occur.\n\nFixes #37056\n\n---\n\n## Problem\n\nWhen embedded agents (subagents) complete their tasks and try to announce results back through the Gateway, they can fail with `network_error` if the Gateway times out (default 60s limit). Unlike channels (Telegram, Discord) which have configurable retry policies, embedded agents had hardcoded retry logic with no configuration options.\n\n---\n\n## Solution\n\nAdded a new `announceRetry` configuration block under `agents.defaults.subagents`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"agents\": {\n    \"defaults\": {\n      \"subagents\": {\n        \"announceRetry\": {\n          \"attempts\": 3,        // Max retry attempts (default: 3, max: 10)\n          \"minDelayMs\": 5000,   // Minimum delay between retries (default: 5000)\n          \"maxDelayMs\": 30000,  // Maximum delay cap with exponential backoff (default: 30000)\n          \"jitter\": 0.1         // Random jitter factor 0-1 (default: 0.1)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Changes\n\n1. **types.agent-defaults.ts**: Added `announceRetry` config type to `subagents` interface\n2. **zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts**: Added zod schema for `announceRetry` with validation\n3. **subagent-announce.ts**: \n   - Added `resolveAnnounceRetryConfig()` to read config with defaults\n   - Added `computeRetryDelayMs()` for exponential backoff with jitter\n   - Updated `runAnnounceDeliveryWithRetry()` to accept and use retry config\n\n### Behavior\n\n- On transient errors (gateway timeout, network errors, etc.), retry with exponential backoff + jitter\n- Default: 3 attempts, 5-30 second delays with 10% jitter\n- Log retry attempts at INFO level\n- After exhausting retries, report final failure\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n- [ ] Unit tests pass\n- [ ] Manual testing with simulated gateway timeout\n- [ ] Config validation works correctly\n\n---\n\n## Breaking Changes\n\nNone - This inconsistency means a queue created with a whitespace-padded key (e.g. `\" session1 \"`) is stored under that untrimmed key, but subsequent lookups and clears — which trim to `\"session1\"` — never find it.\n\n**Impact:** Queued followup items accumulate without being drained or cleaned up when the key has surrounding whitespace, causing memory leaks and missed followup deliveries.\n\n## Change type\n\nBug fix — normalize the `key` parameter in `getFollowupQueue` by adding `key.trim()`, matching the behavior of the other two public functions.\n\n## Changes\n\n- **`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.ts`** — Add `const cleaned = key.trim()` in `getFollowupQueue` and use `cleaned` for both `Map.get()` and `Map.set()`\n- **`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.test.ts`** — New test file with 5 cases covering key normalization consistency, cross-function lookup/clear, and empty-key edge cases\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n```ts\nimport { getFollowupQueue, getExistingFollowupQueue, clearFollowupQueue } from \"./state.js\";\n\n// Before fix: queue stored under \"  key  \", lookups use \"key\" → miss\nconst q = getFollowupQueue(\"  key  \", { mode: \"queue\" });\ngetExistingFollowupQueue(\"key\");   // undefined (bug)\nclearFollowupQueue(\"key\");          // 0, queue not cleared (bug)\n\n// After fix: all three functions normalize to \"key\"\n```\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] All 5 new unit tests pass (`npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.test.ts`)\n- [x] Existing test suite unaffected\n- [x] Linter passes with 0 warnings\n\n## Security\n\nNo security impact. This is a key-normalization consistency fix.\n\n## Compatibility\n\nFully backward-compatible. Keys that were already trimmed behave identically. resolution, so SecretRef-backed channel config could:\n- crash `openclaw status`, `openclaw status --all`, `openclaw channels status`, `openclaw channels resolve`, and doctor/config repair flows\n- collapse `configured but unavailable` into `not configured`\n- skip some read-only security/account summaries when command-path secrets were unavailable\n\nThis PR adds command-local SecretRef resolution for read-only commands, introduces read-only account inspection for built-in channel plugins, and migrates the affected status/channels/doctor surfaces onto that model.\n\n## What changed\n\n- Added command-local SecretRef resolution modes and diagnostics for read-only command paths.\n- Added read-only account inspection for Telegram, Discord, and Slack.\n- Migrated `status`, `status --json`, `status --all`, `channels status`, `channels resolve`, and the relevant doctor/config-summary flows to use inspection/degraded read-only behavior.\n- Preserved `configured but unavailable in this command path` state in both human and JSON status surfaces.\n- Kept channel security audit coverage when supported channel credentials are SecretRef-configured but unavailable in the current command path.\n- Tightened generic channel snapshot projection so read-only JSON surfaces do not pick up unrelated fields like webhook URLs or public keys unless a plugin explicitly adds them.\n- Documented the new read-only behavior and the optional `inspectAccount(...)` hook for plugin authors.\n\n## Scope boundary\n\nThis PR does **not** weaken runtime SecretRef behavior.\n\nRuntime startup/reload/send/auth paths remain strict and fail-fast. DMs would occasionally be duplicated when using preview streaming (the default mode). The first message would appear with an \"(edited)\" indicator, and a second, identical message would be posted immediately after.\r\n\r\n## Root Cause\r\n\r\nThe duplication was caused by a race condition and a missing cleanup step in the final reply delivery logic within `src/slack/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts`.\r\n\r\n1. **Race Condition**: The decision to finalize a draft message via `chat.update` (the `canFinalizeViaPreviewEdit` check) was made before ensuring that the draft stream's throttled send operation had completed. If the final delivery callback was invoked while the initial draft message send was still in-flight, `draftStream.messageId()` would return `undefined`. This caused `canFinalizeViaPreviewEdit` to be `false`, leading the code to fall back to `deliverNormally()`, which posts a new message. The original draft message, once its send operation completed, would then also appear, resulting in a duplicate.\r\n\r\n2. **Missing Cleanup**: In cases where `canFinalizeViaPreviewEdit` was `false` for reasons other than the race condition (e.g., an error payload, or a text-only reply where the draft stream failed), the code would fall through to `deliverNormally()` without clearing the existing draft message. The original implementation only cleared the draft for media payloads (`mediaCount > 0`), leaving other fallback paths vulnerable to creating duplicates.\r\n\r\n## Solution\r\n\r\nThis fix addresses both issues with targeted changes to the `deliver` callback in `dispatch.ts`:\r\n\r\n1. **Synchronize Draft Stream**: An `await draftStream.flush()` is now called before reading `draftMessageId` and `draftChannelId`. This ensures any pending send/edit operations are complete, guaranteeing that the message IDs are available and up-to-date, thus preventing the race condition.\r\n\r\n2. **Generalize Draft Cleanup**: The condition to trigger draft cleanup has been broadened from `mediaCount > 0` to `hasStreamedMessage`, covering all fallback scenarios including text-only replies.\r\n\r\n3. **Deferred Cleanup (Post-Delivery)**: Draft deletion is now performed **after** `deliverNormally()` succeeds, not before. This ensures that if `deliverNormally` fails (e.g., during a Slack API outage), the draft message remains visible so the user still sees a response rather than an empty DM.\r\n\r\n4. **Preserve `status_final` Message**: The `status_final` branch now sets `hasStreamedMessage = false` before its try block, so the post-delivery cleanup correctly skips the status message, which is intentionally preserved alongside the final reply.\r\n\r\n## Changed Files\r\n\r\n| File | Change |\r\n|------|--------|\r\n| `src/slack/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts` | Flush draft stream before finalize check; defer draft cleanup to after successful delivery; preserve `status_final` message |\r\n","number":37012,"title":"fix(slack): prevent duplicate messages in DMs from streaming fallback","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/37012"},{"body":"## Source Issue\n- Issue: #36990\n- URL: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36990\n\n## Original Issue Description\nThe issue introduces Clawguard and provides the original project summary, scope, and links in the source issue body.\n\nCloses #36990","number":37011,"title":"[Issue #36990] [Security] Clawguard: OpenClaw skills/plugins scanner & guard (open-source)","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/37011"},{"body":"## Source Issue\n- Issue: #36987\n- URL: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36987\n\n## Original Issue Description\nThe issue reports incorrect `deliveryContext.to` formatting in Feishu leading to dropped replies; However, `Dirent.isDirectory()` returns `false` for symlinks — so a symlink like `ln -s ~/my-plugin ~/.openclaw/extensions/my-plugin` is silently ignored (no warning, no error).\n\n**Fix:** After the `isFile()`/`isDirectory()` checks, test `isSymbolicLink()` and call `fs.statSync()` (which follows symlinks) to determine the real type. Broken symlinks are skipped silently. Valid symlinks to directories or files are handled identically to real directories/files.\n\nThis matches the existing behavior of `plugins.load.paths` config entries, which use `fs.statSync()` and already follow symlinks.\n\n## Changes\n\n- `src/plugins/discovery.ts`: resolve symlink target type via `fs.statSync` in the `discoverInDirectory` loop\n- `src/plugins/discovery.test.ts`: add test `\"discovers symlinked plugin directories (#36754)\"` that creates a real plugin dir and symlinks it into the extensions directory\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] `pnpm test -- src/plugins/discovery.test.ts` — 13 tests pass (up from 12)\n- [x] New test confirms symlinked plugin directories are discovered\n- [x] Existing security tests still pass (hardlink rejection, world-writable block, symlink escape block)","number":36989,"title":"Plugins: follow symlinks in extension directory scanning (#36754)","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36989"},{"body":"## Problem\nFeishu long-running requests can occasionally finish without sending a reply. In practice this can happen when the gateway channel health monitor restarts the Feishu provider as \"stale-socket\" during an active run, which aborts the in-flight work and drops the final outbound message.\n\nThis is easiest to hit when Feishu is quiet for long stretches (no inbound events), but a user triggers a long task: the channel had no runtime \"busy\" / run-activity signal for the health policy to short-circuit, so it may be restarted mid-run.\n\n## Fix\n- Wire the Feishu extension into the shared run-state machine so active runs patch the gateway runtime with `busy`, `activeRuns`, and a `lastRunActivityAt` heartbeat.\n- Surface transport lifecycle in runtime status (`connected`, `lastEventAt`).\n- Record inbound/outbound activity timestamps for better observability (`lastInboundAt`, `lastOutboundAt`).\n\nThis keeps the health monitor from restarting Feishu while it is actively running work, and makes it easier to debug channel activity from `openclaw channels status --json`.\n\n## Tests\n- `pnpm vitest extensions/feishu/src/channel.test.ts`\n- `pnpm vitest extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`\n- `pnpm vitest extensions/feishu/src/monitor.startup.test.ts`\n- `pnpm vitest extensions/feishu/src/monitor.webhook-security.test.ts`\n","number":36988,"title":"feishu: mark long-running runs as busy to prevent The gateway state was recoverable, but the ownership drift was bad enough to break SSH checks on the host. The current migration doc says `rsync -a` in general, so it is easy to copy the wrong ownership model into a new machine.\n\n## Tests\n- `git diff --check`\n- manual docs review for `docs/install/migrating.md` and `docs/zh-CN/install/migrating.md`\n- did not run `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` because this is a docs-only change\n\n## Real-world validation\n- validated on my live deployment recovery on March 6, 2026 after hitting ownership drift while moving OpenClaw state between machines\n\n## Issue\n- none - docs follow-up from a real migration incident\n\n## AI-assisted\n- yes\n- testing level: lightly tested\n","number":36979,"title":"docs(install): warn about owner-preserving rsync on migration","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36979"},{"body":"## Summary\n\nWhen `systemctl --user is-enabled` returns 'not-found' on WSL2, Node.js execFile populates stderr with the error message `Command failed: systemctl ...` instead of the actual stdout output 'not-found'.\n\nThis causes `isSystemdUnitNotEnabled()` and `isSystemctlMissing()` to fail to recognize the not-found status, throwing an error during gateway service installation on WSL2.\n\n## Fix\n\nPrioritize stdout over stderr in `readSystemctlDetail()`, only using stderr when stdout doesn't contain valid systemctl output (i.e., the generic \"Command failed\" message).\n\n## Testing\n\n- All 24 systemd tests pass\n\n## Related\n\n- Fixes #36939","number":36978,"title":"fix(daemon): handle systemctl not-found output in WSL2","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36978"},{"body":"## Summary\n\nFixes #36811 — `NO_REPLY` sentinel leaks as `NO` in Telegram channels.\n\n**Root cause:** When the agent streams `NO_REPLY`, the streaming layer transiently emits the `NO` prefix fragment via `onPartialReply`. This fragment is queued in the Telegram draft stream via `updateDraftFromPartial`. The `minInitialChars` debounce (30 chars) normally prevents short text from being sent. However, when `stop()` is called during cleanup (e.g. when a silent reply is normalized), it sets `state.final = true` and flushes — which bypasses the `minInitialChars` guard — causing `NO` to be sent as a real Telegram message.\n\n**Fix:** In `updateDraftFromPartial`, check `isSilentReplyPrefixText` for both `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN` (`NO_REPLY`) and `HEARTBEAT_TOKEN` before queuing any text into the draft stream. This prevents partial fragments from entering the draft queue where they could be flushed at finalization.\n\n## Changes\n\n- `src/telegram/bot-message-dispatch.ts`: import `isSilentReplyPrefixText`, `SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN`, `HEARTBEAT_TOKEN`; add guard in `updateDraftFromPartial` to skip silent-reply prefix fragments\n- `src/telegram/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`: add test asserting that `NO_REPLY` partial fragments (`\"NO\"`, `\"NO_\"`, `\"NO_REPLY\"`) never reach `draftStream.update`\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] `pnpm test -- src/telegram/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts` — 59 tests pass\n- [x] New test `\"does not send NO_REPLY partial fragments to the draft stream (#36811)\"` confirms the fix","number":36977,"title":"Telegram: suppress NO_REPLY partial fragments from reaching draft stream (#36811)","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36977"},{"body":"extended the os detection to detect the default OSTYPE=linux under opensuse leap/thumbleweed and SLES added detection for zypper when installing requirements\r\n\r\n## Summary\r\n\r\nDescribe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:\r\n\r\n- Problem: no support for zypper \r\n- Why it matters: script fails\r\n- What changed: added detection for zypper packagemanager\r\n- What did NOT change (scope boundary): nothing else\r\n\r\n## Change Type (select all)\r\n\r\n- [ X ] Bug fix\r\n- [ X ] Feature\r\n- [ ] Refactor\r\n- [ ] Docs\r\n- [ ] Security hardening\r\n- [ ] Chore/infra\r\n\r\n## Security Impact (required)\r\n\r\n- New permissions/capabilities? The fix is purely additive defense-in-depth.\n\n## Change Type (select all)\n\n- [x] Bug fix\n- [ ] Feature\n- [ ] Refactor\n- [ ] Docs\n- [ ] Security hardening\n- [ ] Chore/infra\n\n## Scope (select all touched areas)\n\n- [ ] Gateway / orchestration\n- [ ] Skills / tool execution\n- [ ] Auth / tokens\n- [ ] Memory / storage\n- [ ] Integrations\n- [ ] API / contracts\n- [ ] UI / DX\n- [x] CI/CD / infra\n\n## Linked Issue/PR\n\n- Closes #36939\n\n## User-visible / Behavior Changes\n\n- `openclaw gateway install` on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 no longer fails with `systemctl is-enabled unavailable` when the service unit doesn't exist\n\n## Security Impact (required)\n\n- New permissions/capabilities? `No`\n- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`\n- New/changed network calls? `No`\n- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`\n- Data access scope changed? `No`\n\n## Repro + Verification\n\n### Environment\n\n- OS: Windows 10 WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04\n- Runtime: Node.js 22+\n- Integration/channel: gateway service install\n\n### Steps\n\n1. Run `openclaw gateway install`\n\n### Expected\n\n- Installation proceeds normally (service not found → install)\n\n### Actual\n\n- Before fix: throws `systemctl is-enabled unavailable: Command failed: ...`\n- After fix: returns `false` (not enabled) and proceeds with installation\n\n## Evidence\n\n```\n ✓ src/daemon/systemd.test.ts (25 tests) 7ms\n\n Test Files  1 passed (1)\n      Tests  25 passed (25)\n```\n\nNew test verifies: WSL2 scenario where exit code 1 and stdout contains `not-found` with generic error message correctly returns `false`.\n\n## Human Verification (required)\n\n- Verified scenarios: not-found on stdout with exit code 1, not-found with exit code 4, disabled status, permission denied (still throws)\n- Edge cases checked: empty stdout (falls through to existing throw), whitespace-only stdout\n- What I did **not** verify: live WSL2 environment (no Windows access)\n\n## Compatibility / Migration\n\n- Backward compatible? `Yes` — only changes the error→false path for a specific status\n- Config/env changes? `No`\n- Migration needed? `No`\n\n## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)\n\n- How to disable/revert: revert this commit; workaround is to manually create the systemd unit file\n- Files/config to restore: `src/daemon/systemd.ts`\n- Known bad symptoms: `systemctl is-enabled unavailable` error during gateway install\n\n## Risks and Mitigations\n\n- Risk: overly broad matching could return `false` when it should throw → mitigated by reusing the existing `isSystemdUnitNotEnabled` function which only matches known non-enabled states\n\n","number":36955,"title":"fix(daemon): handle systemctl is-enabled not-found status from stdout on WSL2","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36955"},{"body":"## Source Issue\n- Issue: #36939\n- URL: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36939\n\n## Original Issue Description\n\n## Description\n\nWhen installing OpenClaw gateway service on Windows 10 WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04), the installation fails with the following error:\n\n```\nGateway service check failed: Error: systemctl is-enabled unavailable: Command failed: systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service\n```\n\n## Environment\n\n- **OS**: Windows 10\n- **WSL**: WSL2 with Ubuntu 24.04\n- **systemd**: Enabled and working correctly\n- **OpenClaw version**: 2026.3.2\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Enable systemd in WSL2 (via `/etc/wsl.conf` with `systemd=true`)\n2. Verify systemd is working: `systemctl --user status` shows `State: running`\n3. Run: `openclaw gateway install` or `openclaw gateway install --force`\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\nThe command should recognize that the service is not installed (not-found) and proceed with installation.\n\n## Actual Behavior\n\nThe command throws an error and exits.\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\n\nThe issue is in the `readSystemctlDetail` function in [`src/daemon/systemd.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/daemon/systemd.ts):\n\n```typescript\nfunction readSystemctlDetail(result: { stdout: string; stderr: string }): string {\n  return (result.stderr || result.stdout || "").trim();\n}\n```\n\nWhen `systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service` returns `not-found`:\n\n1. The command outputs `not-found` to **stdout**\n2. The command returns exit code 1 (non-zero)\n3. Node.js `execFile` generates an error with message `Command failed: systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service`\n4. Since **stderr is empty**, the [`execFileUtf8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/daemon/exec-file.ts) function uses the error message as stderr\n5. `readSystemctlDetail` prioritizes stderr over stdout, returning `Command failed: ...` instead of `not-found`\n6. The `isSystemdUnitNotEnabled` function cannot recognize `not-found` status, so it throws an exception\n\n## Verification\n\nRunning the command directly in WSL:\n\n```bash\n$ systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service\nnot-found\n$ echo $?\n1\n```\n\nThe output `not-found` is a valid state indicating the service unit does not exist, which should be handled gracefully.\n\n## Suggested Fix\n\nModify `readSystemctlDetail` to prioritize valid systemctl output over the error message:\n\n```typescript\nfunction readSystemctlDetail(result: { stdout: string; stderr: string }): string {\n  const stdout = result.stdout?.trim() ?? "";\n  const stderr = result.stderr?.trim() ?? "";\n  // Prefer stdout if it contains valid systemctl output (not the generic "Command failed" message)\n  if (stdout && !stdout.toLowerCase().includes("command failed")) {\n    return stdout;\n  }\n  return stderr || stdout;\n}\n```\n\n## Workaround\n\nUsers can manually create the systemd service unit file:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user\ncat > ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service << 'EOF'\n[Unit]\nDescription=OpenClaw Gateway\nAfter=network-online.target\nWants=network-online.target\n\n[Service]\nExecStart=/usr/local/bin/openclaw gateway --port 18789\nRestart=always\nRestartSec=5\n\n[Install]\nWantedBy=default.target\nEOF\n\nsystemctl --user daemon-reload\nsystemctl --user enable --now openclaw-gateway.service\n```\n\nRefs #36939","number":36954,"title":"[Issue #36939] Gateway service check failed on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04: systemctl is-enabled returns not-found but throws error","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36954"},{"body":"## Source Issue\n- Issue: #36935\n- URL: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36935\n\n## Original Issue Description\n\n## Description\n\nWhen the agent uses `[[reply_to_current]]` tags in Slack DM replies, duplicate messages appear in the channel. This is a cross-boundary credential exposure risk (plugin boundary -> host config secrets).\n\n## Reproduction sketch\n1. Create a plugin that logs/exports `api.config.models.providers` inside `register(api)`.\n2. Configure a provider with embedded auth values (e.g. API key/header-based auth) in OpenClaw config.\n3. Load plugin.\n4. Observe provider auth material is accessible to plugin runtime.\n\n## Impact\n- Credential disclosure to untrusted plugin code\n- Potential outbound exfiltration if plugin has network/tool access\n\n## Suggested fix\n1. In plugin loader, redact provider auth-bearing fields before passing `config` into plugin API.\n   - Candidate allowlist approach: expose only non-secret provider metadata (`model`, `baseUrl` if safe), redact `apiKey`, auth headers, tokens, and secret-ref internals.\n2. Add unit tests that assert plugin runtime cannot read provider credential fields.\n3. Document plugin config visibility contract in plugin security docs.\n\n## Notes\n- This issue is a hardening follow-up to PR #36217, not a blocker for unrelated functionality.\n- If maintainers prefer, this can be handled in a separate minimal security PR to avoid branch conflict.\n\nRefs #36917","number":36948,"title":"[Issue #36917] [SEC] Plugin runtime config still exposes provider auth Description\n\n## Bug Description\n\nThe Control UI webchat shows the reading indicator (three dots / typing animation) permanently after the assistant completes its response. Users must manually refresh the page to see the completed response.\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Open the Control UI webchat\n2. Send any message\n3. Wait for the assistant to finish responding\n4. The reading indicator (three dots) remains visible indefinitely\n5. Refreshing the page reveals the completed response\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\n\nThe issue is a **runId mismatch** between the client-generated idempotency key and the server-assigned runId.\n\n### In `Ep` (chat.send handler):\n```js\nconst l = ti(); // generates a new UUID as idempotencyKey\ne.chatRunId = l;\ne.chatStream = "";       // empty string, NOT null\ne.chatStreamStartedAt = o;\n// ...\nawait e.client.request("chat.send", { ..., idempotencyKey: l });\n```\n\n### In `Ip` (chat event handler):\n```js\nif (t.runId && e.chatRunId && t.runId !== e.chatRunId) {\n    // Server's runId !== client's idempotencyKey\n    if (t.state === "final") {\n        // Message gets added to chatMessages, BUT:\n        // chatStream, chatRunId, chatStreamStartedAt are NEVER cleared\n        return n && !As(n) ? (e.chatMessages = [...e.chatMessages, n], null) : "final";\n    }\n    return null; // delta events also silently dropped\n}\n```\n\n### In `a$` (view builder):\n```js\nif (e.stream !== null) {\n    // chatStream is "" (empty string from Ep, never cleared to null)\n    // So this branch always triggers:\n    e.stream.trim().length > 0\n        ? /* show streaming text */\n        : /* show reading indicator (dots) ← STUCK HERE */\n}\n```\n\n### Summary\n- Client sets `chatRunId` to a locally-generated UUID (the idempotency key)\n- Server responds with chat events using its own `runId`\n- The mismatch causes the `"final"` handler to skip clearing `chatStream`/`chatRunId`/`chatStreamStartedAt`\n- `chatStream` remains as `""` (empty string, not `null`), so the reading indicator renders indefinitely\n\n## Suggested Fix\n\nIn the `Ip` function, when `runId` mismatches and `state === "final"`, also clear the streaming state:\n\n```js\nif (t.runId && e.chatRunId && With 83,000+ bindings (enterprise DingTalk, 9,000+ per-user agents), this causes 10+ second delays per message.\n- **Why it matters:** Enterprise deployments with thousands of per-user routing bindings become unusable — every inbound message triggers a full array scan before routing can begin.\n- **What changed:** Added a lazily-built `ChannelAccountIndex` (Map<channel, Map<accountKey, EvaluatedBinding[]>>) that groups all bindings by (channel, accountKey) on first access. On subsequent lookups, the exact-account and wildcard buckets are merged in O(k) time where k is the matching result size, instead of scanning all n bindings.\n- **What did NOT change:** The `EvaluatedBindingsIndex` (byPeer, byGuild, etc.) and downstream routing logic are untouched. The per-(channel, account) result cache is preserved. Default behavior and binding resolution semantics are identical.\n\n## Change Type (select all)\n\n- [x] Bug fix\n- [ ] Feature\n- [ ] Refactor\n- [ ] Docs\n- [ ] Security hardening\n- [ ] Chore/infra\n\n## Scope (select all touched areas)\n\n- [x] Gateway / orchestration\n- [ ] Skills / tool execution\n- [ ] Auth / tokens\n- [ ] Memory / storage\n- [ ] Integrations\n- [ ] API / contracts\n- [ ] UI / DX\n- [ ] CI/CD / infra\n\n## Linked Issue/PR\n\n- Closes #36915\n\n## User-visible / Behavior Changes\n\n- No user-visible changes. Routing produces identical results but executes faster for large binding sets.\n\n## Security Impact (required)\n\n- New permissions/capabilities? `No`\n- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`\n- New/changed network calls? `No`\n- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`\n- Data access scope changed? `No`\n\n## Repro + Verification\n\n### Environment\n\n- OS: macOS\n- Runtime: Node.js 20+\n- Integration/channel: any (DingTalk demonstrated in issue)\n\n### Steps\n\n1. Configure 10,000+ bindings with per-user peer routing\n2. Send an inbound message\n3. Observe routing latency\n\n### Expected\n\n- Sub-millisecond routing regardless of binding count\n\n### Actual\n\n- Before fix: ~10s delay with 83,000 bindings (O(n) scan per cache miss)\n- After fix: sub-millisecond (O(1) index build amortized, O(k) merge per lookup)\n\n## Evidence\n\n```\n ✓ src/routing/resolve-route.test.ts (39 tests) 15ms\n\n Test Files  1 passed (1)\n      Tests  39 passed (39)\n```\n\nNew test validates 200 lookups across 10,000 bindings complete in under 3 seconds (actually completes in ~9ms).\n\nAll 38 existing routing tests pass unchanged — the optimization preserves exact binding resolution semantics.\n\n## Human Verification (required)\n\n- Verified scenarios: all 38 existing routing tests (peer, guild, roles, account, wildcard, dmScope, parentPeer, identityLinks)\n- Edge cases checked: empty accountId → default, explicit \"default\" accountId, wildcard \"*\", duplicate dedup via Map, cache eviction at MAX_EVALUATED_BINDINGS_CACHE_KEYS\n- What I did **not** verify: production deployment with 83,000+ bindings (no access to DingTalk enterprise environment)\n\n## Compatibility / Migration\n\n- Backward compatible? `Yes` — same routing results, same cache semantics\n- Config/env changes? `No`\n- Migration needed? `No`\n\n## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)\n\n- How to disable/revert: revert this commit; the pre-index is purely additive\n- Files/config to restore: `src/routing/resolve-route.ts`\n- Known bad symptoms: incorrect agent routing (wrong agentId for a binding match) — existing test suite covers all binding types\n\n## Risks and Mitigations\n\n- Risk: the pre-index uses additional memory proportional to binding count → mitigated by storing only references to already-allocated EvaluatedBinding objects; the index itself is a Map of Maps with string keys\n- Risk: binding order within merged buckets differs from original listBindings order → mitigated by ensuring exact-account bindings come before wildcard bindings (matching original matchesAccountId semantics where exact wins over wildcard); the EvaluatedBindingsIndex (byPeer, byGuild) resolves ties downstream\n\n","number":36931,"title":"fix(routing): add channel+account pre-index to eliminate O(n) binding scan","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36931"},{"body":"## Summary\n\nThis PR fixes issue #36871 where CLI incorrectly splits custom provider keys containing periods (e.g., llama.cpp).\n\n## Changes\n\n- Modified  in  to support:\n  - Standard dot notation:  → \n  - Bracket notation with double quotes:  → \n  - Bracket notation with single quotes:  → \n  - Escaped dots:  → \n\nNow users can set config values for providers with periods in their names:\n```\nopenclaw config set models.providers[\"llama.cpp\"].baseUrl \"http://localhost:8080\"\n```\n\n## Testing\n\n- Added unit tests in \n- All existing CLI config tests pass","number":36928,"title":"fix(config): support bracket notation in config path parsing (#36871)","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36928"},{"body":"## Summary\n\n- **Problem:** WhatsApp outbound message delivery uses a hardcoded 3-attempt linear retry with fixed 500ms backoff increments, with no way for users to tune retry behavior per deployment or account.\n- **Why it matters:** Different deployments have different network conditions and reliability requirements — a home server on flaky WiFi needs more retries with longer delays, while a cloud deployment may want fewer retries with minimal delay to fail fast.\n- **What changed:** Replaced the inline `sendWithRetry` loop in `deliver-reply.ts` with the shared `retryAsync` infrastructure from `src/infra/retry.ts`. Observe 5 retry attempts with exponential backoff starting at 1000ms\n\n### Expected\n\n- Retry count and delays match the configured values\n\n### Actual\n\n- Before fix: always 3 attempts with fixed 500ms/1000ms/1500ms linear backoff\n- After fix: configurable attempts with exponential backoff from `minDelayMs`\n\n## Evidence\n\n```\n ✓ src/web/auto-reply/deliver-reply.test.ts (14 tests) 13ms\n\n Test Files  1 passed (1)\n      Tests  14 passed (14)\n```\n\nNew tests verify:\n- Custom retry config with 5 attempts is respected\n- Non-transient errors are not retried (single attempt)\n- Existing transient retry behavior preserved with explicit jitter: 0\n\n## Human Verification (required)\n\n- Verified scenarios: text retry, media retry, custom retry config, non-transient error skip\n- Edge cases checked: zero jitter for deterministic tests, account-level config override, default fallback\n- What I did **not** verify: live WhatsApp connection failures (requires active session)\n\n## Compatibility / Migration\n\n- Backward compatible? This caused users to see duplicate messages — the main reply in one card and a short notice in another.\n\n**Root cause chain:**\n\n1. `agent-runner.ts` prepends verbose notices to final payloads → returns array\n2. `dispatch-from-config.ts` iterates the array, calling `sendFinalReply()` for each\n3. Feishu `reply-dispatcher.ts` creates a streaming card for the first final, closes it, then creates a **new** streaming card for the second final (because `streaming` was set to `null` after close)\n\n**Gateway log pattern:**\n```\nClosed streaming: cardId=AAA          ← first final closes\nStarted streaming: cardId=BBB         ← second final creates new card (bug)\nClosed streaming: cardId=BBB          ← immediately closes\ndispatch complete (replies=2)\n```\n\n## Fix\n\nAdded a `streamingClosedForFinal` flag that prevents re-creating streaming sessions after a final payload has already been delivered via streaming. Subsequent final payloads fall through to the standard card/message send path instead.\n\n**Changes:**\n- `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts`: Add `streamingClosedForFinal` guard; reset on `onReplyStart`\n- `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: Update test to verify new behavior (second final goes to standalone card)\n\n## Testing\n\n- All 21 reply-dispatcher tests pass\n- Pre-existing `media.test.ts` failures (4 tests, unrelated `timeout` parameter issue) unchanged","number":36909,"title":"feishu: prevent duplicate streaming cards for multi-payload final replies","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36909"},{"body":"## Summary\n\n- Widen all four `*.jsonl` glob patterns in session-logs SKILL.md to `*.jsonl*` so archived `.reset.*` and `.deleted.*` transcripts are included in search results\n- Document the three transcript file types (active, reset, deleted) in the Tips section\n\n## Changes\n\n- `skills/session-logs/SKILL.md`: Updated glob patterns in \"List all sessions\", \"Find sessions from a specific day\", \"Daily cost summary\", and \"Search across ALL sessions\" examples from `*.jsonl` → `*.jsonl*`\n- Added documentation for the three transcript file types with their suffixes\n\n## Why\n\nArchived transcripts created by `/new`, `/reset`, daily auto-reset, and idle expiry use `.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` suffixes. When provided, retry delays use `sleepWithAbort` (cancellable) instead of `sleep`.\n  - `src/infra/retry-policy.ts`: Added `createAiProviderRetryRunner` with defaults: 4 attempts, 1–60s exponential backoff, 15% jitter. Exported `AbortableRetryRunner` type.\n  - `src/infra/retry.test.ts`: Added 5 new tests covering abort signal, 429 retry, overloaded retry, non-transient error pass-through, and retry exhaustion.\n- **What did NOT change:** The existing failover/profile rotation logic in `run.ts`. The `call.answered` event and the `<Connect><Stream>` TwiML are on the same HTTP request for outbound calls, so `onCallAnswered` fires before the stream connects. This causes `playTts` to fall back to TwiML `<Say>` (Polly) and consume `initialMessage`, leaving nothing for the stream's `onConnect` handler.\n- **Why it matters:** Users configuring ElevenLabs or other streaming TTS providers for outbound calls never hear their initial message via the streaming provider — it always falls back to Polly.\n- **What changed:** `maybeSpeakInitialMessageOnAnswered` now returns early when `this.config.streaming?.enabled` is true, deferring initial message delivery to the `onConnect` callback in `webhook.ts` which fires once the media stream is ready.\n- **What did NOT change:** Non-streaming mode (TwiML `<Say>` fallback) continues to work as before. While the parent `~/.openclaw/cron/` directory is `0700` (providing protection in practice), creating files with world-readable permissions is not defense-in-depth and may expose sensitive cron job data (schedules, message content, delivery targets) in environments where the home directory or umask is configured differently.\n\n## Changes\n\n### `src/cron/store.ts`\n- `mkdir` for cron directory: added `mode: 0o700`\n- `writeFile` for temp file: changed from `\"utf-8\"` to `{ encoding: \"utf-8\", mode: 0o600 }`\n- After `copyFile` to `.bak`: added `chmod(..., 0o600)` (best-effort, same try/catch block)\n\n### `src/cron/run-log.ts`\n- `mkdir` for `runs/` directory: added `mode: 0o700`\n- `appendFile` for log entries: changed from `\"utf-8\"` to `{ encoding: \"utf-8\", mode: 0o600 }`\n- `writeFile` in `pruneIfNeeded`: changed from `\"utf-8\"` to `{ encoding: \"utf-8\", mode: 0o600 }`\n\n## Tests Added\n\n- `store.test.ts`: 3 new tests verifying `0700` dir and `0600` file/bak permissions\n- `run-log.test.ts`: 2 new tests verifying `0700` runs dir and `0600` log file permissions","number":36827,"title":"fix(cron): create cron files and directories with restrictive permissions","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36827"},{"body":"## Summary\n\nFixes #36439 — long messages sent through the Synology Chat plugin are silently truncated by the Synology Chat API beyond ~2000 characters.\n\n### Root cause\n\n`sendMessage()` in `client.ts` sends the full text in a single HTTP payload. The Synology Chat API silently truncates at ~2000 chars — no error, no warning, just lost content.\n\nThe existing `textChunkLimit: 2000` in the channel's `outbound` config only applies to the `sendText` path (API-initiated sends), **not** to the webhook reply dispatcher path which calls `sendMessage()` directly.\n\n### Fix\n\n- Added `splitTextForSynology(text, limit)` — splits long text into chunks of 1800 chars max (safety margin below the ~2000 API limit), preferring newline > space > hard-cut boundaries\n- Refactored `sendMessage()` to iterate over chunks, each sent with full retry logic\n- Returns `false` immediately if any chunk fails (no partial delivery without error)\n- Exported `SYNOLOGY_CHUNK_LIMIT` and `splitTextForSynology` for testability\n\n### Why `client.ts` and not `webhook-handler.ts`?\n\nThe reply path goes: `channel.ts` → `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher` → `deliver()` callback → `sendMessage()`. The deliver callback in `channel.ts` returns `null`, so the `if (reply)` check in `webhook-handler.ts` is never reached. Chunking must happen inside `sendMessage()` itself, at the HTTP transport layer.\n\n### Tests\n\n- 8 new unit tests for `splitTextForSynology` (short text, exact limit, multi-chunk join, newline split, space split, hard cut, custom limit)\n- 3 new tests for `sendMessage` chunking (multi-request for long text, single request for short text, failure propagation)\n- Full suite: **94 tests passing**, zero regressions\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] `pnpm vitest run extensions/synology-chat/` — 94/94 passing\n- [ ] Integration test on real Synology NAS (planned before merge)\n\n🤖 Generated with Reading the file into a Buffer via `loadWebMedia` → `readLocalFileSafely`\n2. Passing the Buffer to `uploadFileFeishu` → Lark SDK `client.im.file.create()`\n3. The Lark SDK uses axios with `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`, and axios's form-data serialization layer can corrupt raw Buffers during multipart boundary encoding\n\nThe issue reporter confirmed that direct SDK uploads with `fs.createReadStream()` work fine, while the same file through the OpenClaw pipeline gets corrupted.\n\n## Fix\n\nFor local file paths, we now:\n1. Still call `loadWebMedia` for **path validation and size checking** (security/SSRF guards)\n2. Pass the **resolved file path string** (not the buffer) to `uploadFileFeishu`/`uploadImageFeishu`\n3. These functions already handle string paths by creating `fs.createReadStream()`, which the form-data library serializes correctly\n\nFor remote URLs and direct buffer inputs, the existing buffer-based path is preserved unchanged.\n\n## Tests\n\nAdded 4 new test cases:\n- ✅ Local file uploads use ReadStream (not Buffer)\n- ✅ Local image uploads use ReadStream (not Buffer)\n- ✅ Remote URLs still use Buffer (existing behavior)\n- ✅ Direct `mediaBuffer` still uses Buffer (existing behavior)\n\n## Related\n\n- #32123 — original bug report with detailed investigation\n- Lark SDK issue: https://github.com/larksuite/node-sdk/issues/121 (Buffer vs ReadStream)","number":36810,"title":"fix(feishu): use ReadStream for local file uploads to prevent binary The sequence was:\n\n1. `stop()` → `flush()` → `sendMessageDraft(chatId, draftId, finalText)` — updates the draft in Telegram's input area\n2. `sendMessage(chatId, finalText)` — creates the real message in chat history\n\nBetween steps 1 and 2, Telegram briefly shows **both** the draft (in the input area) and the newly delivered real message, giving the impression of a duplicate reply. Reopening the chat caused Telegram to clear the stale draft, hiding the duplicate.\n\n**Fix**: After `sendMessage` succeeds in `materialize()`, call `sendMessageDraft(chatId, draftId, \"\")` to explicitly clear the draft. This removes the stale input-area copy immediately after the real message is delivered.\n\n## Changes\n\n- `src/telegram/draft-stream.ts`: In `materialize()`, after a successful `sendMessage`, call `resolvedDraftApi` with an empty string to clear the Telegram draft. Wrapped in try/catch — clearing is best-effort and failure is cosmetic.\n- `src/telegram/draft-stream.test.ts`: Added test `\"clears draft after materializing to avoid duplicate display in DM\"` When the inbound file was a GIF, the MIME type `image/gif` was passed unchanged, causing rejection.\n\n## Fix\n\nTwo-file change:\n\n1. **`src/media/image-ops.ts`** — add `convertGifFirstFrameToPng(buffer)`: loads `sharp` with `{ pages: 1 }` (first animation frame only, to keep memory flat for large animated GIFs) and emits PNG.\n\n2. **`src/media-understanding/providers/image.ts`** — before building the base64 payload, check `imageMime === \"image/gif\"` and run the conversion. Falls back silently on failure so the error surfaces through the normal model-response path rather than crashing the pipeline.\n\n## Impact\n\n- Static and animated GIFs sent via Signal (or any other channel) now produce a description instead of an error.\n- Signal's built-in GIF picker (which sends mp4) is unaffected — this only triggers on `image/gif` MIME.\n- No change to PNG / JPEG / WebP / HEIC paths.\n\n---\n🤖 Generated with Claude Code","number":36662,"title":"fix(media): convert GIF to PNG before passing to vision models","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36662"},{"body":"## Summary\n- promote cron schedule cache hits to most-recently-used order\n- keep current cache bound intact while reducing churn-driven recompilation\n- add regression coverage proving hot entries survive max-size churn after a touch\n\n## Why\nUnder high expression churn, FIFO-like eviction can drop frequently reused evaluators, causing avoidable Cron recompilation on hot paths.\n\n## Risk\nLow. real user turns.\r\n\r\n**This was AI-assisted using Claude, but manually tested and reviewed by me (the human).**\r\n\r\n  ## Summary\r\n\r\n  - **Problem:** `updateLastRoute` set `updatedAt` to `Date.now()` on every routing metadata update, even though no user turn occurred. This made idle-reset think the session was still active.\r\n  - **Why it matters:** Sessions that should have been reset after the idle window (e.g. 30 minutes) were kept alive indefinitely by background routing updates, so users got stale context instead of a fresh session.\r\n  - **What changed:** `updateLastRoute` now uses `mergeSessionEntryPreserveActivity` for existing sessions, leaving `updatedAt` untouched so idle-reset evaluates against the real last-turn time.\r\n  - **What did NOT change:** New sessions (no existing entry) still go through `mergeSessionEntry` as before. All other session write paths (`recordInboundSession`, `initSessionState`, etc.) are untouched.\r\n\r\n  ## Change Type (select all)\r\n\r\n  - [x] Bug fix\r\n  - [ ] Feature\r\n  - [ ] Refactor\r\n  - [ ] Docs\r\n  - [ ] Security hardening\r\n  - [ ] Chore/infra\r\n\r\n  ## Scope (select all touched areas)\r\n\r\n  - [x] Gateway / orchestration\r\n  - [ ] Skills / tool execution\r\n  - [ ] Auth / tokens\r\n  - [x] Memory / storage\r\n  - [ ] Integrations\r\n  - [ ] API / contracts\r\n  - [ ] UI / DX\r\n  - [ ] CI/CD / infra\r\n\r\n  ## Linked Issue/PR\r\n\r\n  - Closes #27102\r\n  - Related #\r\n\r\n  ## User-visible / Behavior Changes\r\n\r\n  Sessions that have been idle past the configured `idleMinutes` threshold will now correctly reset on the next inbound message, even if `updateLastRoute` was called in between.\r\n\r\n  ## Security Impact (required)\r\n\r\n  - New permissions/capabilities? `No`\r\n  - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`\r\n  - New/changed network calls? `No`\r\n  - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`\r\n  - Data access scope changed? `No`\r\n\r\n  ## Repro + Verification\r\n\r\n  ### Environment\r\n\r\n  - OS: macOS\r\n  - Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun\r\n  - Model/provider: N/A (session store logic)\r\n  - Integration/channel (if any): Any (repro uses WhatsApp)\r\n  - Relevant config (redacted): `session.reset: { mode: \"daily\", atHour: 4, idleMinutes: 30 }`\r\n\r\n  ### Steps\r\n\r\n  1. Have an existing session that has been idle for longer than `idleMinutes`.\r\n  2. Trigger a routing update via `updateLastRoute` (e.g. inbound message arrives, `recordInboundSession` calls `updateLastRoute` before `initSessionState`).\r\n  3. `initSessionState` evaluates idle reset.\r\n\r\n  ### Expected\r\n\r\n  - Session resets because the last real turn was beyond the idle window.\r\n\r\n  ### Actual (before fix)\r\n\r\n  - Session was kept alive because `updateLastRoute` had bumped `updatedAt` to now.\r\n\r\n  ## Evidence\r\n\r\n  - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after\r\n  - [ ] Trace/log snippets\r\n  - [ ] Screenshot/recording\r\n  - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)\r\n\r\n  Two new tests added:\r\n  - `session.test.ts`: \"stale session resets after updateLastRoute (idle)\" — confirms `initSessionState` still resets an idle session even after `updateLastRoute` runs.\r\n  - `store.session-key-normalization.test.ts`: \"updateLastRoute preserves updatedAt for existing sessions\" — confirms `updatedAt` is not overwritten by routing updates.\r\n\r\n  ## Human Verification (required)\r\n\r\n  - Verified scenarios: Both new tests pass; existing test suite passes (`pnpm test`).\r\n  - Edge cases checked: New session (no existing entry) still gets a proper `updatedAt` via the default `mergeSessionEntry` path.\r\n  - What you did **not** verify: Live multi-channel routing on a running gateway instance.\r\n\r\n  ## Compatibility / Migration\r\n\r\n  - Backward compatible? `Yes`\r\n  - Config/env changes? `No`\r\n  - Migration needed? `No`\r\n\r\n  ## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)\r\n\r\n  - How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert the single commit; the change is isolated to `updateLastRoute` in\r\n  `src/config/sessions/store.ts`.\r\n  - Files/config to restore: `src/config/sessions/store.ts`\r\n  - Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Sessions resetting too aggressively (i.e. routing updates no longer keeping sessions alive when they should — though by design they should not).\r\n\r\n  ## Risks and Mitigations\r\n\r\n  - **Risk:** Edge case where `mergeSessionEntryPreserveActivity` behaves differently from `mergeSessionEntry` for fields beyond `updatedAt`.\r\n    - **Mitigation:** The only difference is timestamp preservation; both functions share the same merge logic otherwise. New test explicitly validates `updatedAt` is preserved.","number":36650,"title":"fix(sessions): preserve activity timestamps in updateLastRoute","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36650"}]

The fix is purely additive defense-in-depth.\n\n## Change Type (select all)\n\n- [x] Bug fix\n- [ ] Feature\n- [ ] Refactor\n- [ ] Docs\n- [ ] Security hardening\n- [ ] Chore/infra\n\n## Scope (select all touched areas)\n\n- [ ] Gateway / orchestration\n- [ ] Skills / tool execution\n- [ ] Auth / tokens\n- [ ] Memory / storage\n- [ ] Integrations\n- [ ] API / contracts\n- [ ] UI / DX\n- [x] CI/CD / infra\n\n## Linked Issue/PR\n\n- Closes #36939\n\n## User-visible / Behavior Changes\n\n- `openclaw gateway install` on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 no longer fails with `systemctl is-enabled unavailable` when the service unit doesn't exist\n\n## Security Impact (required)\n\n- New permissions/capabilities? `No`\n- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`\n- New/changed network calls? `No`\n- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`\n- Data access scope changed? `No`\n\n## Repro + Verification\n\n### Environment\n\n- OS: Windows 10 WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04\n- Runtime: Node.js 22+\n- Integration/channel: gateway service install\n\n### Steps\n\n1. Enable systemd in WSL2 (`/etc/wsl.conf` with `systemd=true`)\n2. Run `openclaw gateway install`\n\n### Expected\n\n- Installation proceeds normally (service not found → install)\n\n### Actual\n\n- Before fix: throws `systemctl is-enabled unavailable: Command failed: ...`\n- After fix: returns `false` (not enabled) and proceeds with installation\n\n## Evidence\n\n```\n ✓ src/daemon/systemd.test.ts (25 tests) 7ms\n\n Test Files  1 passed (1)\n      Tests  25 passed (25)\n```\n\nNew test verifies: WSL2 scenario where exit code 1 and stdout contains `not-found` with generic error message correctly returns `false`.\n\n## Human Verification (required)\n\n- Verified scenarios: not-found on stdout with exit code 1, not-found with exit code 4, disabled status, permission denied (still throws)\n- Edge cases checked: empty stdout (falls through to existing throw), whitespace-only stdout\n- What I did **not** verify: live WSL2 environment (no Windows access)\n\n## Compatibility / Migration\n\n- Backward compatible? `Yes` — only changes the error→false path for a specific status\n- Config/env changes? `No`\n- Migration needed? `No`\n\n## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)\n\n- How to disable/revert: revert this commit; workaround is to manually create the systemd unit file\n- Files/config to restore: `src/daemon/systemd.ts`\n- Known bad symptoms: `systemctl is-enabled unavailable` error during gateway install\n\n## Risks and Mitigations\n\n- Risk: overly broad matching could return `false` when it should throw → mitigated by reusing the existing `isSystemdUnitNotEnabled` function which only matches known non-enabled states\n\n","number":36955,"title":"fix(daemon): handle systemctl is-enabled not-found status from stdout on WSL2","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36955"},{"body":"## Source Issue\n- Issue: #36939\n- URL: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36939\n\n## Original Issue Description\n\n## Description\n\nWhen installing OpenClaw gateway service on Windows 10 WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04), the installation fails with the following error:\n\n```\nGateway service check failed: Error: systemctl is-enabled unavailable: Command failed: systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service\n```\n\n## Environment\n\n- **OS**: Windows 10\n- **WSL**: WSL2 with Ubuntu 24.04\n- **systemd**: Enabled and working correctly\n- **OpenClaw version**: 2026.3.2\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Enable systemd in WSL2 (via `/etc/wsl.conf` with `systemd=true`)\n2. Verify systemd is working: `systemctl --user status` shows `State: running`\n3. Run: `openclaw gateway install` or `openclaw gateway install --force`\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\nThe command should recognize that the service is not installed (not-found) and proceed with installation.\n\n## Actual Behavior\n\nThe command throws an error and exits.\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\n\nThe issue is in the `readSystemctlDetail` function in [`src/daemon/systemd.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/daemon/systemd.ts):\n\n```typescript\nfunction readSystemctlDetail(result: { stdout: string; stderr: string }): string {\n  return (result.stderr || result.stdout || "").trim();\n}\n```\n\nWhen `systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service` returns `not-found`:\n\n1. The command outputs `not-found` to **stdout**\n2. The command returns exit code 1 (non-zero)\n3. Node.js `execFile` generates an error with message `Command failed: systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service`\n4. Since **stderr is empty**, the [`execFileUtf8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/daemon/exec-file.ts) function uses the error message as stderr\n5. `readSystemctlDetail` prioritizes stderr over stdout, returning `Command failed: ...` instead of `not-found`\n6. The `isSystemdUnitNotEnabled` function cannot recognize `not-found` status, so it throws an exception\n\n## Verification\n\nRunning the command directly in WSL:\n\n```bash\n$ systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service\nnot-found\n$ echo $?\n1\n```\n\nThe output `not-found` is a valid state indicating the service unit does not exist, which should be handled gracefully.\n\n## Suggested Fix\n\nModify `readSystemctlDetail` to prioritize valid systemctl output over the error message:\n\n```typescript\nfunction readSystemctlDetail(result: { stdout: string; stderr: string }): string {\n  const stdout = result.stdout?.trim() ?? "";\n  const stderr = result.stderr?.trim() ?? "";\n  // Prefer stdout if it contains valid systemctl output (not the generic "Command failed" message)\n  if (stdout && !stdout.toLowerCase().includes("command failed")) {\n    return stdout;\n  }\n  return stderr || stdout;\n}\n```\n\n## Workaround\n\nUsers can manually create the systemd service unit file:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user\ncat > ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service << 'EOF'\n[Unit]\nDescription=OpenClaw Gateway\nAfter=network-online.target\nWants=network-online.target\n\n[Service]\nExecStart=/usr/local/bin/openclaw gateway --port 18789\nRestart=always\nRestartSec=5\n\n[Install]\nWantedBy=default.target\nEOF\n\nsystemctl --user daemon-reload\nsystemctl --user enable --now openclaw-gateway.service\n```\n\nRefs #36939","number":36954,"title":"[Issue #36939] Gateway service check failed on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04: systemctl is-enabled returns not-found but throws error","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36954"},{"body":"## Source Issue\n- Issue: #36935\n- URL: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36935\n\n## Original Issue Description\n\n## Description\n\nWhen the agent uses `[[reply_to_current]]` tags in Slack DM replies, duplicate messages appear in the channel. on every `.`, which shattered provider keys that contain dots (e.g. `models.providers[\"llama.cpp\"].baseUrl` → `[\"models\",\"providers\",\"\\\"llama\",\"cpp\\\"]\",\"baseUrl\"]` instead of `[\"models\",\"providers\",\"llama.cpp\",\"baseUrl\"]`).\n\n- Replace the simple `split(\".\")` with a state-machine parser that handles both plain dot notation (`foo.bar`) and bracket notation (`foo[\"bar.baz\"]` or `foo['bar.baz']`).\n- Bracket notation can appear at the start (`[\"top.level\"].child`), consecutively (`a[\"b.c\"][\"d.e\"]`), or mixed with dot notation.\n- All existing security guardrails are preserved: `__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` are still blocked in both plain and bracket notation.\n- Error paths for malformed input (unclosed quotes, missing `]`, empty keys, leading/trailing/consecutive dots) are fully covered.\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] New tests added to `src/config/config-misc.test.ts` covering: double-quoted bracket, single-quoted bracket, `src/config/config-misc.test.ts` pass (`pnpm test -- src/config/config-misc.test.ts`).","number":36951,"title":"fix(config): support bracket notation in parseConfigPath for period-containing This is a cross-boundary credential exposure risk (plugin boundary -> host config secrets).\n\n## Reproduction sketch\n1. Create a plugin that logs/exports `api.config.models.providers` inside `register(api)`.\n2. Configure a provider with embedded auth values (e.g. API key/header-based auth) in OpenClaw config.\n3. Load plugin.\n4. Observe provider auth material is accessible to plugin runtime.\n\n## Impact\n- Credential disclosure to untrusted plugin code\n- Potential outbound exfiltration if plugin has network/tool access\n\n## Suggested fix\n1. In plugin loader, redact provider auth-bearing fields before passing `config` into plugin API.\n   - Candidate allowlist approach: expose only non-secret provider metadata (`model`, `baseUrl` if safe), redact `apiKey`, auth headers, tokens, and secret-ref internals.\n2. Add unit tests that assert plugin runtime cannot read provider credential fields.\n3. Document plugin config visibility contract in plugin security docs.\n\n## Notes\n- This issue is a hardening follow-up to PR #36217, not a blocker for unrelated functionality.\n- If maintainers prefer, this can be handled in a separate minimal security PR to avoid branch conflict.\n\nRefs #36917","number":36948,"title":"[Issue #36917] [SEC] Plugin runtime config still exposes provider auth The reading indicator (three dots) remains visible indefinitely\n5. Refreshing the page reveals the completed response\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\n\nThe issue is a **runId mismatch** between the client-generated idempotency key and the server-assigned runId.\n\n### In `Ep` (chat.send handler):\n```js\nconst l = ti(); // generates a new UUID as idempotencyKey\ne.chatRunId = l;\ne.chatStream = "";       // empty string, NOT null\ne.chatStreamStartedAt = o;\n// ...\nawait e.client.request("chat.send", { ..., idempotencyKey: l });\n```\n\n### In `Ip` (chat event handler):\n```js\nif (t.runId && e.chatRunId && t.runId !== e.chatRunId) {\n    // Server's runId !== client's idempotencyKey\n    if (t.state === "final") {\n        // Message gets added to chatMessages, BUT:\n        // chatStream, chatRunId, chatStreamStartedAt are NEVER cleared\n        return n && !As(n) ? (e.chatMessages = [...e.chatMessages, n], null) : "final";\n    }\n    return null; // delta events also silently dropped\n}\n```\n\n### In `a$` (view builder):\n```js\nif (e.stream !== null) {\n    // chatStream is "" (empty string from Ep, never cleared to null)\n    // So this branch always triggers:\n    e.stream.trim().length > 0\n        ? /* show streaming text */\n        : /* show reading indicator (dots) ← STUCK HERE */\n}\n```\n\n### Summary\n- Client sets `chatRunId` to a locally-generated UUID (the idempotency key)\n- Server responds with chat events using its own `runId`\n- The mismatch causes the `"final"` handler to skip clearing `chatStream`/`chatRunId`/`chatStreamStartedAt`\n- `chatStream` remains as `""` (empty string, not `null`), so the reading indicator renders indefinitely\n\n## Suggested Fix\n\nIn the `Ip` function, when `runId` mismatches and `state === "final"`, also clear the streaming state:\n\n```js\nif (t.runId && e.chatRunId && t.runId !== e.chatRunId) {\n    if (t.state === "final") {\n        const n = ir(t.message);\n        if (n && !As(n)) {\n            e.chatMessages = [...e.chatMessages, n];\n        }\n        // Clear streaming state even on runId mismatch\n        e.chatStream = null;\n        e.chatRunId = null;\n        e.chatStreamStartedAt = null;\n        return "final";\n    }\n    return null;\n}\n```\n\nAlternatively, `Ep` could avoid setting `chatRunId` to the idempotency key and instead wait for the server to confirm the actual `runId`.\n\n## Environment\n\n- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.3.2\n- **Platform:** macOS (Darwin 23.6.0)\n- **Model:** gemini-3.1-pro-preview (via Google provider)\n- **UI:** Control UI webchat (localhost)\n\n## Impact\n\nEvery message sent through the With 83,000+ bindings (enterprise DingTalk, 9,000+ per-user agents), this causes 10+ second delays per message.\n- **Why it matters:** Enterprise deployments with thousands of per-user routing bindings become unusable — every inbound message triggers a full array scan before routing can begin.\n- **What changed:** Added a lazily-built `ChannelAccountIndex` (Map<channel, Map<accountKey, EvaluatedBinding[]>>) that groups all bindings by (channel, accountKey) on first access. On subsequent lookups, the exact-account and wildcard buckets are merged in O(k) time where k is the matching result size, instead of scanning all n bindings.\n- **What did NOT change:** The `EvaluatedBindingsIndex` (byPeer, byGuild, etc.) and downstream routing logic are untouched. The per-(channel, account) result cache is preserved. Default behavior and binding resolution semantics are identical.\n\n## Change Type (select all)\n\n- [x] Bug fix\n- [ ] Feature\n- [ ] Refactor\n- [ ] Docs\n- [ ] Security hardening\n- [ ] Chore/infra\n\n## Scope (select all touched areas)\n\n- [x] Gateway / orchestration\n- [ ] Skills / tool execution\n- [ ] Auth / tokens\n- [ ] Memory / storage\n- [ ] Integrations\n- [ ] API / contracts\n- [ ] UI / DX\n- [ ] CI/CD / infra\n\n## Linked Issue/PR\n\n- Closes #36915\n\n## User-visible / Behavior Changes\n\n- No user-visible changes. Routing produces identical results but executes faster for large binding sets.\n\n## Security Impact (required)\n\n- New permissions/capabilities? `No`\n- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`\n- New/changed network calls? `No`\n- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`\n- Data access scope changed? `No`\n\n## Repro + Verification\n\n### Environment\n\n- OS: macOS\n- Runtime: Node.js 20+\n- Integration/channel: any (DingTalk demonstrated in issue)\n\n### Steps\n\n1. Configure 10,000+ bindings with per-user peer routing\n2. Send an inbound message\n3. Observe routing latency\n\n### Expected\n\n- Sub-millisecond routing regardless of binding count\n\n### Actual\n\n- Before fix: ~10s delay with 83,000 bindings (O(n) scan per cache miss)\n- After fix: sub-millisecond (O(1) index build amortized, O(k) merge per lookup)\n\n## Evidence\n\n```\n ✓ src/routing/resolve-route.test.ts (39 tests) 15ms\n\n Test Files  1 passed (1)\n      Tests  39 passed (39)\n```\n\nNew test validates 200 lookups across 10,000 bindings complete in under 3 seconds (actually completes in ~9ms).\n\nAll 38 existing routing tests pass unchanged — the optimization preserves exact binding resolution semantics.\n\n## Human Verification (required)\n\n- Verified scenarios: all 38 existing routing tests (peer, guild, roles, account, wildcard, dmScope, parentPeer, identityLinks)\n- Edge cases checked: empty accountId → default, explicit \"default\" accountId, wildcard \"*\", duplicate dedup via Map, cache eviction at MAX_EVALUATED_BINDINGS_CACHE_KEYS\n- What I did **not** verify: production deployment with 83,000+ bindings (no access to DingTalk enterprise environment)\n\n## Compatibility / Migration\n\n- Backward compatible? `Yes` — same routing results, same cache semantics\n- Config/env changes? `No`\n- Migration needed? `No`\n\n## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)\n\n- How to disable/revert: revert this commit; the pre-index is purely additive\n- Files/config to restore: `src/routing/resolve-route.ts`\n- Known bad symptoms: incorrect agent routing (wrong agentId for a binding match) — existing test suite covers all binding types\n\n## Risks and Mitigations\n\n- Risk: the pre-index uses additional memory proportional to binding count → mitigated by storing only references to already-allocated EvaluatedBinding objects; the index itself is a Map of Maps with string keys\n- Risk: binding order within merged buckets differs from original listBindings order → mitigated by ensuring exact-account bindings come before wildcard bindings (matching original matchesAccountId semantics where exact wins over wildcard); the EvaluatedBindingsIndex (byPeer, byGuild) resolves ties downstream\n\n","number":36931,"title":"fix(routing): add channel+account pre-index to eliminate O(n) binding scan","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36931"},{"body":"## Summary\n\nThis PR fixes issue #36871 where CLI incorrectly splits custom provider keys containing periods (e.g., llama.cpp).\n\n## Changes\n\n- Modified  in  to support:\n  - Standard dot notation:  → \n  - Bracket notation with double quotes:  → \n  - Bracket notation with single quotes:  → \n  - Escaped dots:  → \n\nNow users can set config values for providers with periods in their names:\n```\nopenclaw config set models.providers[\"llama.cpp\"].baseUrl \"http://localhost:8080\"\n```\n\n## Testing\n\n- Added unit tests in \n- All existing CLI config tests pass","number":36928,"title":"fix(config): support bracket notation in config path parsing (#36871)","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36928"},{"body":"## Summary\n\n- **Problem:** WhatsApp outbound message delivery uses a hardcoded 3-attempt linear retry with fixed 500ms backoff increments, with no way for users to tune retry behavior per deployment or account.\n- **Why it matters:** Different deployments have different network conditions and reliability requirements — a home server on flaky WiFi needs more retries with longer delays, while a cloud deployment may want fewer retries with minimal delay to fail fast.\n- **What changed:** Replaced the inline `sendWithRetry` loop in `deliver-reply.ts` with the shared `retryAsync` infrastructure from `src/infra/retry.ts`. Added a `retry` field to the WhatsApp config schema (both root-level and per-account), resolved through the standard `resolveWhatsAppAccount` hierarchy, and threaded it through to the delivery function.\n- **What did NOT change:** The default retry behavior (3 attempts, 500ms base delay, exponential backoff) is preserved. Feishu `reply-dispatcher.ts` creates a streaming card for the first final, closes it, then creates a **new** streaming card for the second final (because `streaming` was set to `null` after close)\n\n**Gateway log pattern:**\n```\nClosed streaming: cardId=AAA          ← first final closes\nStarted streaming: cardId=BBB         ← second final creates new card (bug)\nClosed streaming: cardId=BBB          ← immediately closes\ndispatch complete (replies=2)\n```\n\n## Fix\n\nAdded a `streamingClosedForFinal` flag that prevents re-creating streaming sessions after a final payload has already been delivered via streaming. The `call.answered` event and the `<Connect><Stream>` TwiML are on the same HTTP request for outbound calls, so `onCallAnswered` fires before the stream connects. This causes `playTts` to fall back to TwiML `<Say>` (Polly) and consume `initialMessage`, leaving nothing for the stream's `onConnect` handler.\n- **Why it matters:** Users configuring ElevenLabs or other streaming TTS providers for outbound calls never hear their initial message via the streaming provider — it always falls back to Polly.\n- **What changed:** `maybeSpeakInitialMessageOnAnswered` now returns early when `this.config.streaming?.enabled` is true, deferring initial message delivery to the `onConnect` callback in `webhook.ts` which fires once the media stream is ready.\n- **What did NOT change:** Non-streaming mode (TwiML `<Say>` fallback) continues to work as before. Inbound calls are unaffected (stream connects before `call.answered`).\n\n## Change Type (select all)\n\n- [x] Bug fix\n- [ ] Feature\n- [ ] Refactor\n- [ ] Docs\n- [ ] Security hardening\n- [ ] Chore/infra\n\n## Scope (select all touched areas)\n\n- [ ] Gateway / orchestration\n- [ ] Skills / tool execution\n- [ ] Auth / tokens\n- [ ] Memory / storage\n- [x] Integrations\n- [ ] API / contracts\n- [ ] UI / DX\n- [ ] CI/CD / infra\n\n## Linked Issue/PR\n\n- Closes #36869\n\n## User-visible / Behavior Changes\n\n- Outbound calls with streaming enabled now correctly use the streaming TTS provider (e.g. ElevenLabs) for the initial message instead of falling back to Polly.\n\n## Security Impact (required)\n\n- New permissions/capabilities? `No`\n- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`\n- New/changed network calls? `No`\n- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`\n- Data access scope changed? `No`\n\n## Repro + Verification\n\n### Environment\n\n- OS: macOS\n- Runtime: Node.js 22\n- Integration/channel: voice-call (Twilio)\n\n### Steps\n\n1. WebChat replies were also delivered to iMessage contacts because `dmScope` defaulted to `\"main\"` when not explicitly configured.\n\n## Root Cause\n\nFive runtime sites defaulted `dmScope` to `\"main\"` via `?? \"main\"`, while onboarding correctly defaults new installs to `\"per-channel-peer\"`. After an upgrade that didn't preserve the explicit dmScope setting, the runtime silently fell back to the unsafe `\"main\"` default, causing all channels to share the same session.\n\n## Fix\n\n- Introduce a shared `DEFAULT_DM_SCOPE` constant (`\"per-channel-peer\"`) in `config/types.base.ts`\n- Replace all 5 hardcoded `?? \"main\"` fallbacks with the shared constant\n- Consolidate with the onboarding default (was a separate `ONBOARDING_DEFAULT_DM_SCOPE` constant)\n\n### Files changed (8):\n- `src/config/types.base.ts` — new `DEFAULT_DM_SCOPE` constant\n- `src/infra/outbound/outbound-session.ts` — outbound routing\n- `src/routing/resolve-route.ts` — inbound routing  \n- `src/routing/session-key.ts` — session key generation\n- `src/security/audit-channel.ts` — security audit\n- `src/commands/doctor-security.ts` — doctor checks\n- `src/commands/onboard-config.ts` — consolidated with shared constant\n- `src/commands/onboard-config.test.ts` — updated imports\n\n## Testing\n\n- All 96 existing tests pass (onboard-config: 3, session-key: 14, audit: 79)\n- TypeScript compilation clean\n- No behavior change for users who explicitly set `session.dmScope` in config\n\n## Breaking Change Note\n\nUsers who intentionally relied on the implicit `\"main\"` default (without setting it in config) will now get `\"per-channel-peer\"` behavior. This is the safer default and matches what onboarding has always set for new installs. While the parent `~/.openclaw/cron/` directory is `0700` (providing protection in practice), creating files with world-readable permissions is not defense-in-depth and may expose sensitive cron job data (schedules, message content, delivery targets) in environments where the home directory or umask is configured differently.\n\n## Changes\n\n### `src/cron/store.ts`\n- `mkdir` for cron directory: added `mode: 0o700`\n- `writeFile` for temp file: changed from `\"utf-8\"` to `{ encoding: \"utf-8\", mode: 0o600 }`\n- After `copyFile` to `.bak`: added `chmod(..., 0o600)` (best-effort, same try/catch block)\n\n### `src/cron/run-log.ts`\n- `mkdir` for `runs/` directory: added `mode: 0o700`\n- `appendFile` for log entries: changed from `\"utf-8\"` to `{ encoding: \"utf-8\", mode: 0o600 }`\n- `writeFile` in `pruneIfNeeded`: changed from `\"utf-8\"` to `{ encoding: \"utf-8\", mode: 0o600 }`\n\n## Tests Added\n\n- `store.test.ts`: 3 new tests verifying `0700` dir and `0600` file/bak permissions\n- `run-log.test.ts`: 2 new tests verifying `0700` runs dir and `0600` log file permissions","number":36827,"title":"fix(cron): create cron files and directories with restrictive permissions","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36827"},{"body":"## Summary\n\nFixes #36439 — long messages sent through the Synology Chat plugin are silently truncated by the Synology Chat API beyond ~2000 characters.\n\n### Root cause\n\n`sendMessage()` in `client.ts` sends the full text in a single HTTP payload. The Synology Chat API silently truncates at ~2000 chars — no error, no warning, just lost content.\n\nThe existing `textChunkLimit: 2000` in the channel's `outbound` config only applies to the `sendText` path (API-initiated sends), **not** to the webhook reply dispatcher path which calls `sendMessage()` directly.\n\n### Fix\n\n- Added `splitTextForSynology(text, limit)` — splits long text into chunks of 1800 chars max (safety margin below the ~2000 API limit), preferring newline > space > hard-cut boundaries\n- Refactored `sendMessage()` to iterate over chunks, each sent with full retry logic\n- Returns `false` immediately if any chunk fails (no partial delivery without error)\n- Exported `SYNOLOGY_CHUNK_LIMIT` and `splitTextForSynology` for testability\n\n### Why `client.ts` and not `webhook-handler.ts`?\n\nThe reply path goes: `channel.ts` → `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher` → `deliver()` callback → `sendMessage()`. The deliver callback in `channel.ts` returns `null`, so the `if (reply)` check in `webhook-handler.ts` is never reached. Chunking must happen inside `sendMessage()` itself, at the HTTP transport layer.\n\n### Tests\n\n- 8 new unit tests for `splitTextForSynology` (short text, exact limit, multi-chunk join, newline split, space split, hard cut, custom limit)\n- 3 new tests for `sendMessage` chunking (multi-request for long text, single request for short text, failure propagation)\n- Full suite: **94 tests passing**, zero regressions\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] `pnpm vitest run extensions/synology-chat/` — 94/94 passing\n- [ ] Integration test on real Synology NAS (planned before merge)\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","number":36825,"title":"fix(synology-chat): chunk long messages to prevent silent truncation","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/36825"},{"body":"## Summary\n- make cron event handlers awaitable so scheduler paths can wait for finished-event side effects\n- await the cron run-log append in the gateway instead of firing it off with `void`\n- add a regression test that proves due-job ticks wait for async finished handlers before completing\n\n## Why\nA cron job could finish real work, but the finished run-log write was still fire-and-forget. If the process died in that gap, the run could disappear from `cron/runs/<jobId>.jsonl`, which makes cron history incomplete and makes restart catch-up more likely to replay stale jobs.\n\n## Testing\n- [x] AI-assisted: Codex\n- [x] Fully tested\n- `pnpm build`\n- `pnpm check`\n- `pnpm test`\n- `pnpm exec vitest run src/cron/service.issue-regressions.test.ts Reading the file into a Buffer via `loadWebMedia` → `readLocalFileSafely`\n2. Passing the Buffer to `uploadFileFeishu` → Lark SDK `client.im.file.create()`\n3. The Lark SDK uses axios with `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`, and axios's form-data serialization layer can corrupt raw Buffers during multipart boundary encoding\n\nThe issue reporter confirmed that direct SDK uploads with `fs.createReadStream()` work fine, while the same file through the OpenClaw pipeline gets corrupted.\n\n## Fix\n\nFor local file paths, we now:\n1. Still call `loadWebMedia` for **path validation and size checking** (security/SSRF guards)\n2. Pass the **resolved file path string** (not the buffer) to `uploadFileFeishu`/`uploadImageFeishu`\n3. These functions already handle string paths by creating `fs.createReadStream()`, which the form-data library serializes correctly\n\nFor remote URLs and direct buffer inputs, the existing buffer-based path is preserved unchanged.\n\n## Tests\n\nAdded 4 new test cases:\n- ✅ Local file uploads use ReadStream (not Buffer)\n- ✅ Local image uploads use ReadStream (not Buffer)\n- ✅ Remote URLs still use Buffer (existing behavior)\n- ✅ Direct `mediaBuffer` still uses Buffer (existing behavior)\n\n## Related\n\n- #32123 — original bug report with detailed investigation\n- Lark SDK issue: https://github.com/larksuite/node-sdk/issues/121 (Buffer vs ReadStream)","number":36810,"title":"fix(feishu): use ReadStream for local file uploads to prevent binary
